court-01.case: Mahua Moitra v. Election Commission of India (writ petition, Supreme Court)
court-01.claim: Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra asked the Supreme Court to quash the Commission's order of 24 June 2025 and to stop it from ordering the same revision in other states, LiveLaw reported.
court-01.headline: Trinamool MP Mahua Moitra moves Supreme Court against electoral roll revision in Bihar

court-02.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, Diary No. 35785 of 2025, with six other petitions
court-02.claim: Counsel for ADR and other petitioners mentioned seven petitions against the Bihar revision, and the Court let them be filed during the vacation and listed them for 10 July 2025.
court-02.headline: Petitions against the Bihar revision listed for 10 July

court-03.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
court-03.outlet: Supreme Court of India (judgment of 27.05.2026, 2026 INSC 564, para 10.8)
court-03.claim: The Court issued notice to the Commission and said the petitions raised three questions about its power, its method and the timing before the Bihar election, according to the account in the Court's 2026 judgment.
court-03.headline: Notice issued, and three questions framed

court-04.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
court-04.claim: The Court recorded the Commission's agreement to publish, district by district and searchable by EPIC number, the list of about 65 lakh electors left off the Bihar draft roll with the reason for each.
court-04.headline: The list of 65 lakh names to be published with reasons

court-05.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
court-05.claim: The Court directed the Commission to accept Aadhaar as proof of identity for the Bihar revision and said it is no proof of citizenship.
court-05.headline: Aadhaar to be accepted as the 12th document

court-06.case: W.P.(C) No. 855 of 2025, tagged with Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
court-06.claim: The Supreme Court's judgment of 27 May 2026 records that some petitions, W.P.(C) 855 of 2025 among them, were filed in support of the revision and asked for it to be held at regular intervals.
court-06.headline: A petition in support of the revision

court-07.case: B Sathyanarayanan v. The Chief Election Commissioner and Another, W.P. No. 39744 of 2025, Madras High Court
court-07.claim: A former AIADMK MLA asked the Madras High Court to order a re-verification of 229 booths in T. Nagar, and the Court adjourned the case after the Commission said the revision would begin within a week, LiveLaw reported.
court-07.headline: SIR of Tamil Nadu electoral rolls will begin in a week, Election Commission tells Madras High Court

court-08.case: Public interest litigation on the SIR in West Bengal, Calcutta High Court
court-08.claim: A PIL asked the Calcutta High Court to have the West Bengal revision use the current roll in place of the 2002 roll and to protect booth level officers, and the Court asked the Commission for an affidavit, The Week reported.
court-08.headline: Calcutta High Court asks EC to submit affidavit on PIL challenging SIR in West Bengal

court-09.case: Petitions including the DMK's against the order of 27 October 2025, Supreme Court
court-09.claim: The Court issued notice on the petitions against the second phase in Tamil Nadu and West Bengal and asked the High Courts to hold back their own cases on the revision, The Leaflet reported.
court-09.headline: Supreme Court seeks ECI's response on pleas challenging SIR in Tamil Nadu, West Bengal

court-10.case: State of Kerala v. Election Commission of India, 2025 SCC OnLine Ker 12336, Kerala High Court
court-10.claim: The Kerala government asked the High Court to put off the revision until the local body elections ended, and the Court dismissed the petition because the Supreme Court had asked High Courts to hold back such cases, SCC Online reported.
court-10.headline: Kerala HC refuses to entertain State's plea to defer SIR leaving it open to approach Supreme Court

court-11.case: Petition of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) on booth level officers, Supreme Court
court-11.claim: On a TVK application saying 35 to 40 booth level officers had died under work pressure, the Court suggested that states provide more staff and cut working hours in proportion, National Herald reported.
court-11.headline: Supreme Court issues directions to ease BLO workload in SIR exercise

court-12.case: State of Kerala and political party leaders v. Election Commission of India, Supreme Court
court-12.claim: The Kerala government and leaders of the IUML, Congress and CPI(M) asked for more time for enumeration forms, and the Court put off a decision to 18 December, LiveLaw reported.
court-12.headline: Supreme Court defers plea to extend Kerala SIR deadline, posts on December 18

court-13.case: PIL No. 1272 of 2025, Allahabad High Court
court-13.claim: A PIL asked the Allahabad High Court to apply the Commission's revision guidelines to Uttar Pradesh's panchayat rolls, and the Court dismissed it, LiveLaw reported.
court-13.headline: Allahabad High Court rejects PIL to adopt ECI's SIR guidelines for UP three-tier panchayat roll revision

court-14.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal)
court-14.claim: The Court recorded that about 1.40 crore people in West Bengal had been sent notices and directed that names in the logical discrepancy list be displayed at panchayat, block and ward offices.
court-14.headline: Names in the logical discrepancy list to be displayed

court-15.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal), with Mamata Banerjee's W.P.(C) No. 129 of 2026
court-15.claim: The order records that Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee appeared in her own petition on 4 February 2026, and the Court directed the 8,505 officers the state offered to report to the district officers.
court-15.headline: 8,505 state officers to assist the registration officers

court-16.case: Special civil application by two Surat Congress office-bearers, Gujarat High Court
court-16.claim: The Surat district Congress president and a Seva Dal organiser asked the Gujarat High Court to reject objections not filed under the rules, to act against false objections and to halt the revision, LawTrend reported.
court-16.headline: Gujarat HC moved against voter list revisions

court-17.case: Petition by 91 displaced residents of Akbar Nagar, Lucknow, W.P.(C) No. 191 (as reported), Supreme Court
court-17.claim: Residents displaced by a 2023 demolition said they were left out of the Uttar Pradesh revision, and the Court sent them to the district election officer with liberty to go to the Allahabad High Court, Verdictum reported.
court-17.headline: Supreme Court declines to entertain plea of displaced Lucknow Akbar Nagar residents over voter roll exclusion

court-18.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal)
court-18.claim: The Court recorded the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court's report that over 10,16,000 objections had been disposed of, and directed that appeals against the judicial officers' orders go to tribunals of former Chief Justices and judges.
court-18.headline: Appeals to tribunals of former judges

court-19.case: Suo Motu W.P.(C) No. 3 of 2026, In Re: Safety and Security of Judicial Officers Deputed for Work Relating to SIR of Electoral Rolls in the State of West Bengal
court-19.claim: After seven judicial officers deciding SIR objections were surrounded at a BDO office in Maldah district, the Court directed central forces for them and directed the Commission to give the inquiry to an independent agency such as the CBI or the NIA.
court-19.headline: Court acts after judicial officers are surrounded in Maldah

court-20.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal), with W.P.(C) No. 462 of 2026
court-20.claim: The Court directed that appeals the tribunals decided by 21 or 27 April 2026, before polling, be given effect in a supplementary roll, and said a pending appeal gave no right to vote.
court-20.headline: A pending appeal gives no vote

court-21.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal)
court-21.claim: Counsel told the Court that 136 of nearly 27 lakh appeals had been decided, and the Court declined fresh grievances and sent the parties to the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court, Supreme Court Observer reported.
court-21.headline: West Bengal SIR: SC pushes SIR disputes to Calcutta HC as appeal backlog mounts

court-22.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
court-22.claim: The Court held the Bihar revision lawful under section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act read with Article 324 and said declining to enrol someone does not declare that person not to be a citizen.
court-22.headline: The Supreme Court upholds the Bihar revision

court-23.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
court-23.outlet: Supreme Court of India (2026 INSC 564, para 186(h))
court-23.claim: The Court directed the Commission to refer within four weeks the cases it deleted as non-citizens to the authority under the Citizenship Act and allowed people in Bihar whose names were, in the Court's words, "erroneously deleted" as absent, dead, shifted or duplicate to seek judicial review.
court-23.headline: Citizenship cases to the competent authority, and judicial review for wrong deletions

court-24.outlet: High Court for the State of Telangana (order reproduced by LiveLaw)
court-24.claim: A Charminar voter asked the High Court to restore his family's deleted names, and the Court dismissed the petition and told him to use the revision then under way.
court-24.headline: Deleted voter told to use the SIR

court-25.case: Writ petition by Adivasi Sena, Telangana High Court
court-25.claim: Adivasi Sena asked the Telangana High Court to have non-tribal voters it called ineligible deleted from the rolls of the Fifth Schedule Areas during the revision, and the Court sought replies, Telangana Today reported.
court-25.headline: Telangana HC seeks response on plea against non-tribal voters in Scheduled Areas

court-26.case: Batch of writ petitions on G.O.Ms. No. 172, Telangana High Court
court-26.claim: Petitioners asked the Telangana High Court to strike the state's Family Register Certificate from the revision's list of documents, and the Court gave the Commission time and listed the case for 12 August, Telangana Today reported.
court-26.headline: Telangana HC takes up plea on Family Register Certificate as voter eligibility proof

court-27.case: PIL on homeless and demolition-displaced voters, Delhi High Court
court-27.claim: A PIL asked the Delhi High Court for special arrangements so homeless and displaced people could enrol in the revision, and the Court reserved its order and said it would not monitor the policy, LiveLaw reported. LiveLaw reported on 1 September that the bench of Chief Justice D.K. Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia had dismissed the petition. The Court said the Commission's Manual on Electoral Rolls already provides, in clause 8.5, how a homeless person's ordinary residence is determined, so the fear that homeless people would be left off the draft appeared to be without basis. It said any elector left off the roll after a demolition or relocation can file Form 6.
court-27.response: The Court said the petition gave no particulars or numbers of people displaced by demolitions who remained off the roll. The Commission told the Court that clause 8.5 lets homeless people enrol without documentary proof of residence once a booth level officer has verified over more than one night that they are present at the address given, Bar and Bench reported.
court-27.headline: Delhi SIR: plea to include homeless and demolition-displaced voters

court-28.case: Writ petition by a deleted elector working abroad, Calcutta High Court
court-28.claim: A man deleted in the revision said it was blocking his passport renewal, and the Calcutta High Court told the appellate tribunal to decide his appeal within two weeks without going into the merits, LiveLaw reported.
court-28.headline: Calcutta High Court directs SIR tribunal to expeditiously decide plea of Saudi resident unable to renew passport over voter list deletion

court-29.case: Devender Yadav & Anr v. Election Commission of India & Anr, 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 835, Delhi High Court
court-29.claim: Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav challenged the Form 6 declaration that voters left off the draft must sign as first-time applicants, and he withdrew the petition after the Court told him to file it as a PIL, LiveLaw reported.
court-29.headline: Delhi SIR: High Court refuses to entertain plea against first-time applicant declaration for deleted voters, says file PIL

court-30.case: Petition of two transparency activists under Article 32, Supreme Court
court-30.claim: Two transparency activists who had petitioned the Court asked for the list of Delhi voters sent notices and the criteria for logical discrepancies, and the bench told the Commission to look at extra safeguards, ThePrint reported.
court-30.headline: Delhi SIR: SC says notices going to people mechanically, asks EC to adopt additional safeguards

court-31.case: W.P.(Crl.) No. 401 of 2026, against decisions of the Chief Election Commissioner, Supreme Court
court-31.claim: A petition asked the Court to quash 14 decisions it said the Chief Election Commissioner took alone, and the Court issued notice, tagged it with a similar case and said it had not approved any modified Form 6, LiveLaw reported.
court-31.headline: Supreme Court says modified Form 6 not approved by it

court-32.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
court-32.claim: A family of six told the court that they had moved house within the same constituency and filed Form 8 on a BLO's instruction, and that they were then deleted from the roll because the ERONET software found no record of their cards and allowed only a rejection. The bench asked the Commission to show where the law allows a deletion without a hearing and said the family should not have been asked to file Form 6, The Wire reported, citing The Times of India.
court-32.response: The Wire reported that the Commission's counsel said other voters deleted in the same way had been put back on the roll after filing Form 6, and that the family had not filed Form 6 when asked to.
court-32.headline: 'No Business Asking Them to Fill Form 6 Because System Didn't Allow Form 8': Bombay HC Condemns ECI's Handling of SIR Process

court-33.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
court-33.claim: At a further hearing of the same family's petition the bench asked what purpose the revision served if citizens were left off the roll. It also asked why a voter who had moved house should have to sign the enumeration form, whose declaration says the voter still lives at the address on the existing roll, LiveLaw reported.
court-33.response: LiveLaw reported that the Commission's counsel argued that a voter had to submit the enumeration form along with Form 8 to have an address changed, and that a voter who did not submit it had to file Form 6.
court-33.headline: 'What Is SIR's Purpose If Citizens Are Being Removed From Voter's List? Bombay High Court Asks ECI

court-34.case: Petition on the implementation of the SIR in Maharashtra, Bombay High Court
court-34.claim: The Chief Justice's bench refused an oral request to order that no names be deleted from the roll in Maharashtra for the time being. It said it would follow the Supreme Court, which it was told had restrained High Courts in November 2025 from hearing petitions on the revision, and adjourned the case by four weeks, LiveLaw reported. The petition asks for the order and reasons behind the revision in the state and for safeguards against wrongful exclusion.
court-34.headline: Maharashtra SIR: Bombay High Court Declines Oral Plea To Restrain ECI From Deleting Voters' Names, Says SC Seized Of Issue

court-35.case: MA Baby v. Union of India and others, WP(c) 63560/2026, Supreme Court
court-35.claim: The Supreme Court told the Centre not to stop all trains and Metro services in Delhi before the 10 October protests against the Chief Election Commissioner, and to run them in a regulated way, LiveLaw reported. The petition was brought by CPI(M) General Secretary MA Baby and others against the closure of 57 Metro stations and the cancellation of trains due at New Delhi and Nizamuddin. The order said the notifications appeared to be overreaching, and ETV Bharat reported that the bench also asked the Centre to reconsider Jantar Mantar as the designated protest site.
court-35.response: The order records that the Solicitor General "has fairly agreed to impress upon the authorities to reassess such prohibitions." He said the impression that the whole city had been shut "is far from the truth."
court-35.headline: Don't Completely Stop Trains/Metro In Delhi To Handle October 10 Protests : Supreme Court To Centre

court-36.case: Contempt petition against the Union Home Secretary, the Delhi Police Commissioner and the DMRC chairperson, Supreme Court
court-36.claim: A contempt plea filed in the Supreme Court on 10 October alleged that the Centre and Delhi authorities defied the Court's order of 9 October, keeping 57 Metro stations shut and cancelling Delhi-bound trains before the protest against the Chief Election Commissioner, Outlook reported. The plea also said no traffic advisory had been published in newspapers. A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana listed it to be heard with a petition against the detention of opposition leaders at a special sitting on Sunday 11 October, Bar and Bench reported. On 15 October, before the Chief Justice and Justice Bagchi, the Delhi Police Commissioner filed two affidavits that tendered an unconditional apology for any perceived non-compliance and said there had been no non-compliance with the Court's orders of 9 and 11 October. Justice Bagchi observed that on the Solicitor General's account the apology appeared qualified.
court-36.response: The Solicitor General said the apology was included as standard practice in answering a contempt notice and that the government was defending its actions on facts. The Commissioner asked for the contempt notice to be discharged.
court-36.headline: Supreme Court Contempt Plea Alleges Delhi Authorities Defied Order On Metro, Train Curbs

court-37.case: Application by five deleted electors in the West Bengal SIR matter, Supreme Court
court-37.claim: Five electors deleted from West Bengal's roll after adjudication applied to the Supreme Court for their appeals to be decided before the Kolkata and Howrah municipal elections, LiveLaw reported. They also asked for a Special Investigation Team to examine how the revision's decisions were made. The application cites the Commission's affidavits as showing 1.7 lakh appeals pending from Kolkata and Howrah.
court-37.response: None was reported. The applicants say the Chief Electoral Officer has not published the criteria for logical discrepancies.
court-37.headline: SIR-Deleted Voters Move Supreme Court For Expeditious Disposal Of Appeals Before Kolkata, Howrah Municipal Elections

court-38.case: Application by five deleted electors in the West Bengal SIR matter, Supreme Court
court-38.claim: Counsel for electors deleted from West Bengal's roll after adjudication asked the Supreme Court to hear their plea before the Kolkata and Howrah municipal elections and to let appellants vote, LiveLaw reported. The Chief Justice said the Court would try to list it on 16 October, or else on 29 October, and suggested the tribunals take up appeals for inclusion first and appeals seeking deletion last. Counsel told the Court that nearly 1.70 lakh appeals from the two municipal areas were pending.
court-38.response: No submission by the Commission was reported. The figures put to the Court were counsel's, partly drawn from the Commission's affidavits.
court-38.headline: 'We Are Conscious' : Supreme Court To Consider Plea To Prioritise SIR-Deleted Voters' Appeals Ahead Of Kolkata, Howrah Municipal Elections

court-39.case: Paka Suresh v. Union of India, SLP(C) No. 35786/2026, Supreme Court
court-39.claim: The Supreme Court, hearing a challenge to the Andhra Pradesh High Court's order for local body elections within six weeks, said the elections should use the revised roll if it is published before the polls are notified, and the existing roll if it is not. It said the roll in force applies until the Commission publishes the revised list and that the revision cannot be a reason to delay the polls.
court-39.response: The bench noted that the Election Commission had proposed to publish the final roll on 16 October 2026. Senior counsel for the State Election Commission said the rolls in force continue until the Commission publishes a fresh list. Deccan Chronicle reported on 15 October that the Commission had moved the final publication in Andhra Pradesh to 30 October and the last date for disposing of claims and objections to 22 October. The Wire reported that the YSRCP moved the Supreme Court on 20 October, alleging that violence during the filing of nominations for the state's urban local body elections kept its candidates from taking part.
court-39.headline: Andhra Pradesh Local Body Elections | Conduct Polls As Per Old Rolls If SIR Not Complete Before Notification: Supreme Court

court-40.case: WP 32975 of 2026, a petition by two electors, Telangana High Court
court-40.claim: The Telangana High Court asked the Commission why one petitioner was left off the roll without a notice and what happened to the other after his hearing, LiveLaw reported. The petition challenges notices over minor discrepancies and the automated matching used in the revision. The case was listed again for 13 October. At the hearing of 13 October, senior counsel for the Commission said one petitioner's name had been deleted and he would have to file Form 6, and that the other's petition was premature because the final roll had not been published, Telangana Today reported. He assured the bench that reasoned orders, open to appeal, would be passed where electors on the draft were left off the final roll, provided they attended the hearings on their notices and gave documents. He said that where no order was passed, the elector's name could be taken as included. The case was adjourned to 15 October.
court-40.response: The Commission's counsel sought time for instructions. She said the second petitioner was sent a notice over a mismatch in his father's name and heard on 15 September, and that the first could file Form 6.
court-40.headline: Telangana SIR | Plea Challenges 'AI-Based' SIR Process; High Court Asks ECI Why Voter Was Excluded Without Notice

court-41.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
court-41.claim: The Bombay High Court at Goa adjourned the St Cruz family's petition by a week at the Commission's request, after the Commission said orders the Supreme Court might pass could bear on it. The judges took the view that the Supreme Court's orders may not have a direct bearing, PTI reported, and the Commission's advocate told reporters the Supreme Court had asked High Courts to defer such hearings.
court-41.response: The Commission's counsel also said "what is under challenge is the rejection of Form 8" and that it "cannot be looked at in isolation."
court-41.headline: Goa HC adjourns hearing on plea challenging voter deletion as ECI points out SC cases

court-42.case: Rahul Gandhi v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026 (Diary No. 64196 of 2026), Supreme Court
court-42.claim: Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and other INDIA bloc leaders filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court on 12 October against the Election Commission, the Chief Election Commissioner and the two Election Commissioners. Delhi Police stopped their march to the Court on Bhagwant Das Road, and counsel filed the petition shortly before the filing counter closed. LiveLaw reported that the leaders then went to the Registry, and that a large crowd gathered inside the Court's precincts. The petition asks for the SIR to be suspended in every state while the case is heard, for a committee under a retired Supreme Court judge to audit the names left off or deleted, and for the Commission's files on its decision to hold the revision. PTI reported that the Registry flagged more than ten defects in it, among them illegible or missing pages, an unclear copy of Kharge's identity card and a court fee short by over Rs 200. LawBeat reported that the Registry registered it on 13 October once the defects were cured.
court-42.response: No response from the Commission was reported.
court-42.headline: SC registry points out 10 defects in Rahul Gandhi's plea in SIR case

court-43.case: Rahul Gandhi v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026 (Diary No. 64196 of 2026), Supreme Court
court-43.claim: A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notice on the INDIA bloc leaders' petition to the Election Commission, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, LiveLaw reported. Bar and Bench reported that the bench tagged it with the SIR cases already pending. The Chief Justice said that issuing notice did not mean the Court was condemning anything, and that the Court would ask one of the petitioners about his conduct at the next hearing. He said the petition would be entertained on that petitioner's behalf on a provisional basis, subject to his explaining his conduct. The bench did not name him in court. LiveLaw reported that the written order, uploaded later that day, names him as petitioner no. 6, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut. Notice was also issued on separate petitions by AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi and Congress leader Digvijaya Singh. No interim order was reported. The Hindustan Times had reported on 12 October that the batch of SIR petitions was listed for 27 October. LiveLaw reported on the morning of 27 October that the joint petition was listed that day with two other petitions on the Commission's functioning, before the bench of the Chief Justice, Justice Bagchi and Justice Mohana.
court-43.response: No counsel for the Commission was reported. The Court said "Somebody will accept notice on behalf of the Election Commission of India," Bar and Bench reported.
court-43.headline: 'One Petitioner Has To Explain His Conduct': Supreme Court Issues Notice On INDIA Bloc Leaders' Petition Against ECI Over SIR

court-44.case: W.P.(C) No. 1360 of 2026 (Diary No. 64394 of 2026), a petition by four advocates on the march of 12 October, Supreme Court
court-44.claim: The same bench issued notice on a petition by four advocates about the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court on 12 October, and on a second plea seeking similar relief, LiveLaw reported. The petition asks for rules on demonstrations near the Supreme Court and the High Courts and for criminal contempt proceedings against Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav and Mahua Moitra. Senior counsel for the petitioners said about 200 lawyers had signed a memorandum calling the march browbeating. The Chief Justice said nobody could browbeat the Court and that the judges knew what was said outside it. The Court directed all law enforcement agencies to preserve the CCTV footage and other digital material they had collected, and LiveLaw reported that it also directed footage of the Court's premises to be preserved. Bar and Bench reported that notice went to the Congress, Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders, and that the Court declined to begin contempt proceedings that day.
court-44.response: No reply from the leaders named was reported.
court-44.headline: 'Nobody Can Browbeat Us' : Supreme Court In Plea Against October 12 March By Opposition Leaders; Issues Notice

court-45.case: W.P.(C) 14955/2026, a petition by two electors, Delhi High Court
court-45.outlet: Delhi High Court (order of 14.10.2026, as published by LiveLaw)
court-45.claim: The Delhi High Court closed a petition by two electors whose names were left off Delhi's roll after they moved house and could not fill the enumeration form. They had asked the Court to quash para 4(c) of the SIR guidelines and to change the procedure that requires such electors to seek fresh inclusion through Form 6, and to restore their entries and let them move them to their new address through Form 8. The Commission's standing counsel said they could file Form 6 and that the Electoral Registration Officer would help. The first petitioner said that filing Form 6 would be a false declaration. The bench said that, since the suggestion came from the Commission's counsel on the officer's instructions, his fear of being accused of a false declaration was misplaced. It closed the petition and said the petitioners could file Form 6 if they wished, to be processed in accordance with law. It did not decide the challenge to the guidelines.
court-45.response: The Commission's standing counsel said the grievance could be redressed if the petitioners filed Form 6 under rule 25(2) read with rule 13(1)(a) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and that he had asked the first petitioner to do so at the previous hearing and the Electoral Registration Officer would help.
court-45.headline: Delhi High Court closes a petition by two electors left off the roll and leaves them free to file Form 6

court-46.case: Plea on voter deletions in Maharashtra's SIR, Supreme Court (petitioner and case number not reported)
court-46.claim: The Supreme Court declined to issue notice on 15 October on a plea about deletions in Maharashtra's revision and listed it for 26 October, LawChakra reported. The Chief Justice refused to hear it with the other petitions on the revision and said the Court would take the states one at a time, Maharashtra first and then Delhi. The petition says about 1.2 crore of Maharashtra's 9.79 crore electors were flagged for logical discrepancies, and the Commission had not yet replied. Bar and Bench reported that senior counsel for the petitioner, Arvind Datar, told the Court that 1.2 crore of Maharashtra's 9.79 crore electors had been flagged for logical discrepancies and that 40.6% of electors had been left off the roll in Pune and some other areas. He asked for notice to be issued that day so that the authorities could reply before 26 October, and the Chief Justice said "Not today. Not today."
court-46.response: LawChakra reported that the Election Commission's response was not yet on record. Maharashtra's period for claims and objections ran to 26 October, the day of the hearing.
court-46.headline: Supreme Court Lists Maharashtra SIR Voter Deletions Plea For October 26, Says Matters Cannot Be Generalised

court-47.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals
court-47.claim: The Election Commission had filed appeals before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals against the inclusion of at least 14,75,887 voters by 17 October, 49.2% of the 30,00,545 voters in the records whom judicial officers had examined and found eligible, The Wire reported from appeal records collected by the Civic Research Group. Malda, Murshidabad and Uttar Dinajpur hold 44.6% of these appeals. In the 41 seats where minorities are more than half the population the appeals equal 5.9% of the draft roll, and in the 89 seats where they are under 10% they equal 0.6%. The tribunals had decided 80,091 appeals, or 5.4%, and the report says no tribunal has been able to upload an order since 21 September. In a follow-up on 24 October, The Wire reported that the Civic Research Group's fuller records show 16,08,175 appeals by the Commission against 32,53,401 voters found eligible, 49.4%, close to the 16,10,311 appeals against inclusion that the Commission reported to the Supreme Court in September. It reported that the appeal numbers carry a filing date, a structure that activists found and The Wire says it verified, and that 13,85,374 of the 13,95,794 appeal IDs in an earlier extract of 17 October, or 99.3%, carry one of three dates, 5, 6 or 8 April 2026, with more than 12 lakh on 5 April. The roll was frozen for the Assembly election at midnight on 7 April.
court-47.response: The report says the Commission has not said on what grounds it filed the appeals, who decided to file them, or whether each case was reviewed before an appeal was filed. The follow-up says only the Commission can confirm the dates read from the appeal numbers, and that a single date on more than 12 lakh appeals does not by itself show who authorised them.
court-47.headline: Election Commission Seeks to Remove Half the Bengal Voters Judges Have Cleared For Inclusion

court-48.case: Application by two transparency activists in their pending petition on the Delhi SIR, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, Supreme Court
court-48.claim: Two transparency activists who had petitioned the Court on the Delhi revision filed an application against the requirement that electors left off Delhi's draft apply again on Form 6, whose declaration says the applicant is applying for inclusion for the first time, LiveLaw reported. The application says 47,56,722 electors, 32.78% of those on the roll before the revision, were left off the draft, and that a false declaration can be punished under section 31 of the 1950 Act. It asks for a way to restore these electors without that declaration, and for the additional declaration form added to Forms 6 and 8 through the SIR guidelines to be declared without the force of law because it was not made under section 28 of the Act. Counsel asked the Court to let them use Form 8 or another form. On 14 October the bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi moved the hearing of the main petition from 30 to 28 October.
court-48.response: No submission by the Commission was reported. Counsel told the Court that 30 October was the last date in Delhi for correcting deletions.
court-48.headline: Delhi SIR: Supreme Court Advances Hearing After Plea Flags Deleted Voters Being Asked To Fill Form 6

court-49.case: A fresh writ petition on the modified Form 6, Supreme Court (petitioner not reported)
court-49.claim: On a fresh writ petition, the bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said its remarks of 5 October meant only that the modified Form 6 did not exist when the Bihar case was heard, and that the Court had neither approved nor disapproved it, Bar and Bench reported. Counsel for the petitioner had said the Commission was presenting the altered form as approved by the Court. The Hindustan Times reported that the bench said it would examine the issue and listed the petition with the batch of SIR petitions on 27 October, when it would also take up the wider challenge to how the Commission's decisions on the revision were taken.
court-49.response: The Commission's press note of 26 September said the Supreme Court had upheld the additional declaration attached to Form 6 for the revision. The Hindustan Times reported that the Commission maintains the statutory form itself was not altered and that the declaration is an addendum for the revision only. In its affidavit of 26 October in the Supreme Court, the Commission said Form 6 had not been amended and that the SIR declaration is a separate document, Bar and Bench reported (court-52).
court-49.headline: We have neither approved nor disapproved ECI's Form 6 modification: Supreme Court clarifies

court-50.case: PIL by an advocate for an expert committee on the Election Commission, Supreme Court
court-50.claim: An advocate filed a PIL in the Supreme Court asking for an independent expert committee, chaired by a former Chief Justice or judge of the Court, to examine shortcomings in the functioning of the Election Commission, Bar and Bench reported. It relies on The Indian Express report of 23 September that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi recorded written objections at least 14 times over ten months to decisions taken by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar alone. Citing reports of a Commission affidavit, it says about 38.20 lakh appeals had been filed in West Bengal by people excluded from the roll and about 1.02 lakh decided. It also asks the Commission to bar campaigning on religious tags, religious symbols and communal appeals. No hearing date was reported.
court-50.response: The plea says the Commission acknowledged the dissenting notes and described them as routine suggestions. The plea describes all the West Bengal appeals as filed by people excluded from the roll. The Commission's own count splits them into 22,21,118 appeals by people found not eligible and 16,10,311 appeals against inclusion.
court-50.headline: Plea before Supreme Court seeks expert committee headed by former CJI to examine ECI's functioning

court-51.case: W.P.(C) No. 1330 of 2026, a petition on voter deletions in Maharashtra's SIR, Supreme Court
court-51.claim: The Supreme Court issued notice to the Election Commission on 26 October on a petition against deletions in Maharashtra's revision and listed it for 5 November, and the Chief Justice orally assured that no elector deleted in the revision would be prosecuted for applying again through Form 6, The Hindu and LawChakra reported. The Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana declined to extend the period for claims and objections, which closed that day, or to stop the final roll before hearing the Commission. Senior advocate Arvind Datar, for the petitioner, said thousands of electors in Mumbai and Pune were marked absent and then deleted because their old buildings were being redeveloped and they had moved out, and he put the redevelopment projects at 3,500 in Mumbai and 1,500 in Pune. He said electors who had been deleted were being made to file Form 6 as new voters, which he said is an offence, and asked for a new form to be notified for electors deleted in the revision. LawChakra reported that he also said about 3 crore of the state's roughly 9 crore electors had been deleted after the draft, 1.22 crore of them for a logical discrepancy, and that about 40% were missing from the rolls in Pune and Mumbai. ANI reported the Chief Justice as saying the Court could extend the date later if it found people who had yet to file their documents.
court-51.response: The Commission's reply is awaited. LawChakra says the Court recorded no finding on the petitioner's figures. The assurance on Form 6 was given orally in court.
court-51.headline: Supreme Court assures no deleted voters will be prosecuted for submitting Form 6

court-52.case: A petition seeking a writ of quo warranto against the Chief Election Commissioner, on which notice was issued on 5 October 2026, heard with W.P.(Crl.) No. 401 of 2026, Supreme Court
court-52.claim: The Election Commission filed a short affidavit in the Supreme Court on 26 October in reply to a petition seeking a writ of quo warranto against the Chief Election Commissioner over how the Commission's decisions are taken, and said the affidavit was approved by a unanimous decision of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, Bar and Bench reported. The affidavit says files go to one Election Commissioner, then to the other and then to the Chief Election Commissioner, and that a suggestion, observation or query by a member during this process is not a decision of the Commission under Section 18 of the 2023 Act. It says that in urgent cases members approve electronically and the approval is recorded on the file later. It says the three SIR orders of 24 June 2025, 27 October 2025 and 14 May 2026 were unanimous decisions of the Commission. It says Form 6 has not been amended, because only the Central Government can amend it, and that the SIR declaration is a separate document. It accepts that the way the declaration was shown online could be read as an amendment, and says this was done so that an applicant needs a single OTP and e-sign. By a decision of the Commission's ER Division of 21 October 2026 the online application is to be in two parts, as the paper forms are. It says the appeals in West Bengal against the inclusion of electors were filed by officers of the state Chief Electoral Officer under the Court's orders and were not placed before the Commission. It says the Commission decided on 26 September 2026 that Booth Level Officers will collect documents from the homes of unmapped electors, who need not be called to a hearing, and that hearings will be held only in exceptional cases, preferably online. Item iii of the Commission's press note ECI/PN/120/2026 of 26 September 2026 reads "The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon’ble Supreme Court." The affidavit, as Bar and Bench reported it, says the SIR declaration is a separate document. LiveLaw reported that the petitions were listed before the bench of the Chief Justice, Justice Bagchi and Justice Mohana on 27 October. The Indian Express, which reported the affidavit on 27 October, said it was approved for filing by a unanimous decision of all three members and reported further points. The affidavit accepts that the way the declaration appeared online "could be construed as though an amendment of Form 6 had been made" and that "certain steps taken by the officers" needed "to be corrected". It says the Electoral Registration Officer remains the statutory authority for the roll and that "no entry is added or deleted or modified except by order of the Electoral Registration Officer". It sets out a committee that includes experts from IIT Mumbai and IISc Bengaluru to review whether ECINet complies with the law, as decided by the Commission on 26 and 30 September, and the scrutiny of new IT modules before they are approved. It says 88 of the 97 Goa electors left off the final roll have since applied through Form 6. It says the West Bengal appeals were filed by officers in the state Chief Electoral Officer's office, citing a letter from that office of 22 October. It says an order by which a senior officer redistributed work among the Commission's officers was never implemented after the two Election Commissioners' joint direction, and that the letters the two Commissioners wrote were about that order.
court-52.response: This is the Commission's own account, given on oath. The Commission filed a short reply because of the Dussehra vacation and asked for liberty to file a detailed reply paragraph by paragraph. The affidavit does not say how many West Bengal appeals were filed, who in the Chief Electoral Officer's office approved them, or on what grounds, Bar and Bench reported. The Indian Express's analysis says the affidavit does not say who approved the online change to Form 6 in July, two months after two of the three members had recorded in writing that it should not be made. It says the affidavit presents the ECINet committee as the Commission's decision of September without mentioning Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi's proposal of 29 May, does not explain why Goa's registration officers could not act on their decisions in the software in February, and does not reconcile its West Bengal account with Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu's note that the state's Chief Electoral Officer told him she had no information about the appeals. On the July order, the paper says the affidavit does not say why it was issued without the Commission, why the file was withheld from a member of the Commission, or what has happened to the officer, who is not named.
court-52.headline: No change to Form 6; members' approval obtained electronically in urgent matters: ECI to Supreme Court

court-53.case: W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026, the petition seeking a writ of quo warranto against the Chief Election Commissioner, heard with the connected petitions on the Commission's functioning, among them W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026, Supreme Court
court-53.claim: The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana adjourned the batch of petitions on the Election Commission's functioning on 27 October and gave the petitioners 10 days to file rejoinders to the Commission's affidavit of 26 October (court-52), LiveLaw reported. LiveLaw reported that the bench tentatively listed the matter on 17 November. Senior Advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, for Rahul Gandhi and the INDIA bloc leaders (court-43), asked the Court to order that file notings and internal communications be preserved. The Chief Justice replied that the Court knew everything and would examine it. No order to preserve the records was reported. Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy, for Trinamool Congress MP Dola Sen, said the affidavit accepted many of the charges in Sen's petition about the online Form 6, and that the Commission had issued a press note saying the Court had authorised the change. Bar and Bench reported that she told the Court it had done no such thing. LiveLaw's live page records the Chief Justice saying that the Court was issuing notice on her petition. No interim order was reported.
court-53.response: Senior Advocate Maninder Singh, for the Commission, objected to Guruswamy's submissions. Bar and Bench reported that he said "I represent the Election Commission. They are following rhetoric for some other purpose," and that Solicitor General Tushar Mehta called the request to preserve the file notings an unfair request.
court-53.headline: 'We Will Examine': Supreme Court Adjourns Pleas Alleging Unilateral ECI Decisions

court-54.case: The petition of two transparency activists on the Delhi SIR, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, and their application on Form 6 (court-30, court-48), Supreme Court
court-54.claim: The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana asked the Election Commission on 28 October why electors left off Delhi's draft for not returning enumeration forms are asked to apply on Form 6, which is meant for first-time voters, when they were on the roll of 2026, LiveLaw reported. Justice Bagchi said the Commission's four categories leave no place for electors who were never served a form, such as someone away from Delhi for a month, and that if the roll of 2026 is the base an elector who has shifted should be allowed Form 8. The bench suggested a residual category for those temporarily away, asked the Commission to reach out to electors given Delhi's floating population, and, as Bar and Bench reported, said the excluded names must be easily accessible in simple Hindi and local languages. Bar and Bench also reported Justice Bagchi saying the Court had not finally decided whether the logical discrepancy exercise is lawful, and had allowed it in West Bengal only as an interim arrangement. Counsel for the petitioners, Prashant Bhushan, said 43 of the 47 lakh left off are shown as permanently shifted or absent. The Indian Express reported that the bench said electors left off the draft who had only been away for a time should be allowed to submit the enumeration form, and those who had moved to another address in Delhi should be allowed Form 8. The Chief Justice suggested a statement or circular saying that Form 6 is to be filled only by those registering as voters in Delhi for the first time, LiveLaw and The Indian Express reported, and The Indian Express reported him adding that it was not for those on the roll of 2026 who could not fill the enumeration form because they had moved or were away. Hindustan Times reported the Court asking for a public notice saying that Form 6 is for first-time enrolment and that those who had moved could use Form 8 or the enumeration form. The Chief Justice also told the Commission not to go by any cut-off date while no election is due in Delhi, to keep inviting Form 6 and Form 8 and verify the documents attached, and to issue a public notice in newspapers and online that the process is continuing, The Indian Express reported. The Times of India reported the bench's suggestion that the Commission publish the list of electors left off with the reason against each name, ask them to contact the nearest booth level officer and fill Form 8, give them enumeration forms and tell them they may fill either Form 6 or Form 8. The bench listed the matter after two weeks. The Indian Express reported that the bench said it was not issuing an order to extend the deadline of 30 October and expected the Commission to act on its own, and The Times of India reported that the bench spoke without passing any order. No written order was reported. Anjali Bhardwaj, one of the two petitioners, wrote on X on 30 October that the Court had said electors on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors should be allowed to fill the enumeration form or Form 8 in place of Form 6, which she wrote requires them to make a false declaration that they are first-time voters. She wrote that 32 lakh of the 47 lakh on that list in Delhi were marked permanently shifted and 12 lakh untraceable or absent.
court-54.response: Senior Advocate Dama Seshadri Naidu, for the Commission, said the authorities would examine the concerns, take remedial steps and consider extending the deadline, LiveLaw reported. He said the roll of 2026 before the revision is the base. Bar and Bench reported that the Commission would consider accepting late enumeration forms and would extend the deadline of 30 October if needed. The Indian Express reported Naidu telling the bench that the Commission would report its steps in two weeks and that the time would be extended in the meanwhile. The Times of India reported him saying that the Commission had held more than one lakh camps in Delhi, that not a single person had come to fill Form 8, and that no one had been prosecuted for using Form 6 to restore a name.
court-54.headline: Delhi SIR : Why Deleted Voters Asked To File Form 6 When They Were On 2026 Rolls? Supreme Court Asks ECI

court-55.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals in Samserganj and Sujapur (court-47)
court-55.claim: In Sujapur, in Malda district, the Election Commission has filed appeals against the inclusion of 61,066 of the 1,07,690 electors whom judicial officers examined and found eligible, 56.7%, The Wire reported. It said that is more appeals than in any other seat in West Bengal. The figures come from appeal records collected by the Civic Research Group. In Samserganj, in Murshidabad district, judicial officers found 74,775 electors not eligible, the most of any seat, and the Commission has appealed against 15,195 of the 33,152 they cleared, 47.6%. The Wire reported that 72,838 of the 76,156 pending appeals in the two seats, 96%, carry one timestamp of 5 April 2026, two days before the roll was frozen for the Assembly election, and that their numbers run in sequence one roll part at a time, which it reads as appeals generated in batches. It reported that 99.9% of the electors appealed against in Samserganj and 99.6% in Sujapur have names it describes as recognisably Muslim, a classification it says it estimated from Bengali names and not from official records. It said the Commission did not single them out from among those cleared, because almost everyone the judges cleared in both seats has such a name. The tribunals had decided 105 of the 76,261 appeals in the two seats. In Sujapur the appeals equal almost a quarter of the draft roll of 2,56,276 and slightly exceed the winning margin of 60,287 in April, and in Samserganj they are about twice the margin of 7,587.
court-55.response: The report says the Commission has not said on what grounds it is challenging these electors, whether each case was reviewed before an appeal was filed, why so many appeals share one timestamp, or why it has appealed against about half or more of those cleared. No reply from the Commission is reported.
court-55.headline: Two Bengal Seats, 72,000 ECI Appeals, One Timestamp: 99% of Target Voters Are Muslim

court-56.case: Petitions on the Kerala SIR, heard with the SIR matters concerning Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh (up-26), Supreme Court
court-56.claim: The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant declined on 30 October to extend the time for the revision in Kerala and said that corrections and inclusions in the roll are a continuing process, Times Now Navbharat reported. Counsel for the petitioners said many people could not submit their enumeration forms for want of time. The Chief Justice asked them to identify the people who should still be given a chance and bring them to the Election Commission's notice by representation, and said the Court would ask the Commission to examine them and keep the matter pending. The Commission agreed to consider such representations and to file a report in the Court. Senior Advocate Datar gave the Court a note for the petitioners, saying they had raised the exclusion of names at a large scale, that the Commission should file a detailed affidavit, and that the matter cannot be treated as infructuous only because the revision is over. The bench gave the Commission four weeks to file its counter affidavit in the main matter and to answer the points in the note.
court-56.response: Counsel for the Commission said the revision was complete and that electors can still apply for corrections because the process is continuous, Times Now Navbharat reported.
court-56.headline: केरल में SIR की समयसीमा बढ़ाने से सुप्रीम कोर्ट का इनकार, कहा- सुधार और नाम जोड़ने की प्रक्रिया जारी रहेगी

court-57.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals against electors cleared by judicial officers (court-47, court-55)
court-57.claim: Subrata Gupta, the Election Commission's special roll observer for West Bengal's revision, told The Wire that the observers had no information that the Chief Electoral Officer's office had filed appeals against electors whom judicial officers had examined and found eligible. He said the observers' role ended with the supplementary rolls, which listed about 33 lakh electors the judicial officers retained and 27 lakh they deleted, that he had heard that many of the 27 lakh deleted had appealed for inclusion and that the observers had no access to those records, and that they had heard of the appeals against inclusion only informally, with no official communication. The Commission told the Supreme Court in September that 16,10,311 such appeals had been filed. Its counter affidavit of 26 October (court-52) said a letter of 22 October from the Chief Electoral Officer's office stated that the office's officers had filed them as authorities under the Representation of the People Act. The Wire reported that Gupta, a retired IAS officer of the 1990 batch, now advises Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari.
court-57.response: The Wire says it has written to the Chief Electoral Officer and the Additional Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal asking which officers filed the appeals, on whose decision and on what grounds. No reply is reported.
court-57.headline: Bengal SIR Observer Says He Knew Nothing About CEO Office's 16 Lakh Appeals Against Cleared Voters

court-58.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals in Hemtabad (court-47, court-55)
court-58.claim: In Hemtabad, a seat reserved for Scheduled Castes in Uttar Dinajpur district, the Election Commission has filed appeals against 15,381 of the 34,327 electors whom judicial officers examined and found eligible, 44.8%, The Wire reported. The appeal records were collected and verified by the Civic Research Group and given to The Wire, which says it analysed and verified them again. Of the 13,776 pending appeals, 12,758 carry the code that activists read, and The Wire says it verified, as the batch lodged on the evening of 5 April 2026, 978 carry the code for 6 April, and 40 were filed online. The paper reported that 599 of the appeals with the 5 April code concern electors cleared in the constituency's twelfth and last supplementary list, which was published on 6 April, so the appeals were on record before the list that cleared those electors was made public. The 599 come from nine polling stations, and 162 of them from part 237. Of the 2,65,162 electors on Hemtabad's draft roll, 52,542 were placed under adjudication, and judicial officers struck 18,215 off the roll and found 34,327 eligible. By The Wire's classification of names, which counts the elector's own name or a relative's, at least 97.7% of the electors appealed against have Muslim names, as do all 599, and at least 97% of all those the judges cleared do, so the appeals largely mirror who was cleared. The report says the Commission's appeal rate in the seat is close to its statewide rate of 49.4%. The tribunals have marked the other 1,605 of the seat's appeals disposed of.
court-58.response: The report says the records cannot show whether the judicial officers' decisions were already on the Commission's portal before the list was published. The Commission told the Supreme Court on 26 October that officers of the office of the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer filed the appeals (court-52), and the report says it has not said which officers or on what grounds. No reply from the Commission is reported.
court-58.headline: In One Bengal Seat, EC Appealed Against 599 Voters Even Before Their Adjudication Result Was Published

court-59.case: Reference of electors to judicial officers in West Bengal's revision under the Supreme Court's orders (court-57, soft-42)
court-59.claim: The Election Commission's statewide Notice and Hearing Report dated 22 February, seen by The Wire, records that when the deadline for deciding hearing cases passed on 21 February, West Bengal's Electoral Registration Officers and their assistants had cleared 1,31,45,109 of 1,51,92,634 cases for the final roll, 86.5%, found 11,58,636 ineligible, 7.6%, and left 8,88,889 undecided, 5.9%, The Wire reported. The final roll of 28 February placed 60,06,675 electors under adjudication, and The Wire says at least 51 lakh of them had already been decided by a registration officer. In the report the Electoral Roll Micro Observers marked 31,43,868 cases 'documents need to be reviewed' and the roll observers marked 40,28,055, some of them the same cases. Where the registration officers acted on these flags they disagreed with the observers in 35,92,292 cases and agreed in 2,02,926. Across the 24 districts The Wire finds that the number placed under adjudication rises and falls with the observers' flags, with a correlation of 0.95, and that the observers' flags bear little relation to the number of cases the registration officers left undecided, with a correlation of 0.26. In Malda 8,730 cases were left undecided and 8,28,127 electors were placed under adjudication, and in Murshidabad the figures were 12,194 and 11,01,145. In Uttar Dinajpur 4,80,341 were placed under adjudication against 2,75,074 observer flags.
court-59.response: The Wire quotes the Chief Electoral Officer's office as saying on 1 March that names were marked under adjudication 'since the concerned EROs/AEROs did not decide them after hearing'. Subrata Gupta, the Commission's special roll observer, told it that the Commission had told observers that about 90 lakh of about 1.5 crore cases heard had been disposed of and 60 lakh were pending. The Wire says it has sent the Chief Electoral Officer queries on who decided to send cases the registration officers had already decided to the judges, and that it will update the report on a reply.
court-59.headline: How Over 50 Lakh Cleared West Bengal Voters Ended Up Under Judicial Review In SIR

court-60.case: The petition of Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri on the Delhi SIR, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, and IA No. 317050 of 2026, Supreme Court (court-54)
court-60.outlet: Letter of the petitioners to the Chief Election Commissioner, and ECI letter No. 23/2026-ERS (Vol.-II), both of 03.11.2026, as Prashant Bhushan posted them on X
court-60.claim: Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, the two transparency activists who are the petitioners in the Supreme Court case on Delhi's revision, wrote to the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, on 3 November 2026, with a copy to Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer, Ashok Kumar, asking for immediate compliance with what they call the Court's directives at the hearing of 28 October (court-54). Their letter says the bench observed that forcing voters "deleted during SIR" to fill Form 6, which contains the declaration of being a first-time voter, is an error, and that the judges termed it a "structural incongruity". It says that of the 47 lakh electors left off Delhi's draft and placed on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors, 31.59 lakh were marked permanently shifted and 11.73 lakh untraceable or absent. The letter says the Court orally directed that those marked as having shifted residence be allowed to fill Form 8, and said that the 11.73 lakh marked absent or untraceable should be allowed to fill enumeration forms even at this stage and not be forced to enrol as new voters on Form 6. It asks the Commission and Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer to set up and publicise a simple way to do this, with clear instructions to accept Form 8 and enumeration forms from electors on the list without making them submit Form 6, and it notes that the Commission has extended Delhi's timeline. On the same day the Commission wrote to the Chief Electoral Officers of every state and union territory that an elector whose name is not in the draft roll has to seek inclusion afresh, may do so on Form 6, and is not to face action under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 only because the elector was on an earlier roll, provided the elector is not enrolled in any other constituency and the declaration is otherwise in accordance with law. The Commission's letter does not mention Form 8, the enumeration form, the petitioners' letter or the Supreme Court hearing. Prashant Bhushan, counsel for the petitioners, posted both letters on X on 3 November and wrote that "in response to our letter asking EC to allow shifted votes to fill form 8, the ECI issued orders to force shifted voters to fill form 6 (with an assurance that they will not be prosecuted for false declaration)". The Hindu reported both letters the same day.
court-60.response: The Commission's letter No. 23/2026-ERS (Vol.-II) of 3 November 2026 says: "The submission of Form 6 in such circumstances is, therefore, for the purpose of inclusion in the electoral roll under SIR or afterwards and is not, by itself, false merely because the elector was previously enrolled." It cites the Delhi High Court's order of 14 October 2026 (court-45) and names no other court proceeding.
court-60.headline: The petitioners in the Delhi case ask the Commission to accept Form 8 and enumeration forms, and the Commission clarifies Form 6 the same day

court-61.case: The petition of Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri on the Delhi SIR, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, Supreme Court (court-54, court-60)
court-61.claim: Prashant Bhushan, counsel for the petitioners in the Delhi case, mentioned the matter before a bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, on 4 November and said electors left off the draft feared prosecution if they filed Form 6 with its declaration that they were enrolling for the first time, although the Commission's letter of 3 November says no action will be taken on that ground alone (court-60), Hindustan Times and The Hindu reported. He said the letter went against what the Court had said at the hearing of 28 October (court-54), and that the Commission had extended the time for claims and objections in Delhi to 25 November. The Chief Justice asked how electors could be afraid when the Court was hearing the matter, told the petitioners to file an application, and said the Court would hear it on 19 November, the date the matter is already listed for. The Court passed no urgent order. The Hindu reports that the Chief Justice said the case would be heard after the Deepavali holidays, and that the bench said the Commission could be asked to extend the date further if required.
court-61.response: The Commission's letter No. 23/2026-ERS (Vol.-II) of 3 November 2026 says no action under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 is to be started against an elector only because the elector was on an earlier roll and filed Form 6, provided the elector is not enrolled in another constituency (court-60). Neither report gives anything said for the Commission at the mentioning.
court-61.headline: SIR: Don’t fear, Supreme Court tells Delhi voters struck off draft electoral roll

court-62.case: A petition by a group of advocates for guidelines on processions and protests near the Supreme Court, after the march of 12 October against the Chief Election Commissioner (court-44)
court-62.claim: A bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, on 3 November sought replies from the Congress president, Mallikarjun Kharge, and Rahul Gandhi, and from the Centre, on a petition by a group of advocates about the Opposition's march to the Supreme Court on 12 October against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, and listed it for 23 November, Hindustan Times reported. The petition seeks guidelines regulating processions, protests, demonstrations and assemblies near the Court. The senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia, for the petitioners, told the Court that the march drew a large gathering of lawyers and supporters into the court precincts. He alleged in court that Gandhi pushed a woman journalist who was three months pregnant and that she had to be taken to hospital, and he moved an application for an FIR against Gandhi. These are allegations made for the petitioners, and the report gives no order of the Court on that application. The Solicitor General, Tushar Mehta, said the Centre would reply by the next date and asked that the matter be heard with a petition by the Network of Women in Media, India on alleged sexual harassment of women journalists covering protests in Delhi. The petition also names Akhilesh Yadav, the Delhi Commissioner of Police, the Supreme Court registry and the Congress as respondents.
court-62.response: The senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, for Gandhi and Kharge, said their replies would be filed soon and asked that "irresponsible statements should not be made before the court takes up the matter".
court-62.headline: SC seeks Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge’s replies on plea over Opposition march against CEC to top court

court-63.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
court-63.outlet: Bombay High Court at Goa (judgment of 5.11.2026, as published by LiveLaw)
court-63.claim: The Bombay High Court at Goa on 5 November allowed the petition of a family of six from Santa Cruz who had moved house within the constituency, filed Form 8 and were left off the draft roll and the final roll (court-32, court-33, court-41). A bench of Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit S. Jamsandekar held that section 22 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and rule 13 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 stay in force during a special intensive revision, and that a registration officer who receives Form 8 is bound to decide it. It held that the family were not new voters and could not be told to file Form 6. It also held that Form 6, the pre-filled enumeration form and the declaration in Annexure D to the guidelines would each have made them give a false declaration open to prosecution under section 31. The registration officer rejected their Form 8 on 21 January 2026, two days after claims and objections closed, with no formal order, no reasons and no hearing. The court found that the only reason was that ERONET was frozen during enumeration and gave the officer one option, which was to reject. It held that this amounted to a suspension of section 22 and rule 13 and was impermissible. It allowed the petition against the rejection and the two appeal orders that upheld it, and directed the registration officer of Santa Cruz to include the six in Part 25 of the roll within ten days, after confirming their residence. It made no order as to costs. It declined to keep the petition pending until the Supreme Court decides the challenges to the revision, because the family had not challenged the revision itself. The Times of India reported on 13 November that the six were back on the roll of Santa Cruz with their original EPIC numbers, and that Goa's Chief Electoral Officer, Sanjay Goel, said they had been included in the draft roll published on 12 November, as the court directed.
court-63.response: For the Commission, Gaurish Agni and, at later hearings, the senior advocate Ashutosh Kumbhakoni argued that the family's Form 8 was rightly rejected because they had refused to fill the pre-filled enumeration form and hand it to the booth level officer at their old address, that they were new voters in relation to the draft roll and had to file Form 6 with the Annexure D declaration, and that the portal for processing forms was frozen during enumeration. After the judgment was pronounced the Commission's advocate, Gaurish Agni, asked for a stay of at least two weeks so that the Commission could challenge it in the Supreme Court. The bench refused because its directions concern including the petitioners in the roll. Dainik Gomantak TV reported on 6 November that Agni said the Commission is moving the Supreme Court against the order. The Times of India reported on 13 November that one of the six had filed a caveat in the Supreme Court, in anticipation of an appeal by the Commission, so that no stay would be passed without his being heard. It did not report an appeal by the Commission. Goa's Chief Electoral Officer, Sanjay Goel, told O Heraldo his office would study the order, implement it if it could be implemented, and challenge it if there was scope to.
court-63.headline: Bombay High Court at Goa orders a Santa Cruz family of six onto the roll within ten days and refuses the Commission a stay

court-64.case: Petitions by Manoj Jha and an advocate challenging section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, Supreme Court
court-64.claim: A bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission on 4 November on petitions challenging section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, and listed them for 18 December, The Hindu and The Indian Express reported. Section 16 bars every court from entertaining or continuing any civil or criminal proceedings against a serving or former Chief Election Commissioner or Election Commissioner for any act, thing or word in the discharge of official duty. The Hindu reports that the petitions were filed by the RJD Member of Parliament Manoj Jha and by an advocate. The petitions argue that the section bars the jurisdiction of the constitutional courts and interferes with judicial review, which has been held to be part of the basic structure of the Constitution. The advocate's plea, as The Hindu quotes it, says the section bars all kinds of prosecution, gives immunity for life and covers acts that may be outside lawful authority. The petitions point out that the President and the Governors are protected from criminal proceedings only while in office. The advocate's plea, as The Indian Express quotes it, says a voter whose name is wrongly deleted from the roll is left without a remedy, and it cites the paper's reports of alleged differences between the Chief Election Commissioner and the two Election Commissioners over the SIR. The Indian Express reports that the Court is already hearing a petition by the NGO Lok Prahari against the same section, in which it issued notice in January and declined to stay the section.
court-64.response: Neither report gives anything said for the Centre or the Commission at the hearing. The advocate's plea says the section was added to the Bill by an amendment that gave no reasons for it, and that the Minister's justification in Parliament did not show it was needed.
court-64.headline: SC seeks Centre, EC response on law giving blanket, lifelong immunity to CEC, Election Commissioners

court-65.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals against electors cleared by judicial officers (court-47, court-55, court-58)
court-65.claim: The Wire's classification of the names in appeal records compiled by the Civic Research Group finds that at least 14,39,797 of the 16,08,175 electors against whose inclusion the Election Commission has appealed, after judicial officers examined them and found them eligible, have Muslim names, 89.5%. The report gives Muslims as 27% of West Bengal's population in the 2011 Census and about 29% of its electorate. Grouping seats by the minority share of their population, The Wire finds Muslim names among 61.7% of the electors appealed against in the 89 seats where that share is under 10%, 83.8% in the 71 seats at 10% to 20%, 90.3% in the 51 seats at 20% to 30%, 93.8% in the 39 seats at 30% to 50% and 96.6% in the 41 seats over 50%. In every group the Commission appealed against between 46.5% and 51.2% of the electors the judges cleared, and the report says that across seats there is almost no relationship between a seat's Muslim share and the share of its cleared electors appealed against. It counts 137 constituencies where at least 90% of the electors appealed against have Muslim names, and 2,62,416 electors with Muslim names facing appeals in the 160 seats where Muslims are under a fifth of the population. In Purba Medinipur district, where it gives the Muslim share of the population as 12.0%, 92.9% of the 27,091 electors appealed against have Muslim names, and in Purba Bardhaman, at 23.3%, 95.9% of 90,637 do. In Murshidabad the figure is 98.2%. In Krishnaganj in Nadia, a seat reserved for Scheduled Castes, Muslim names are 157 of the 2,412 electors appealed against, 6.5%, against a population share of 5.7%, and in Jadavpur they are 125 of 881, 14.2%, against 1.2%. The report also uses a second set of records, of appeals by electors whom judicial officers deleted, and does not say who compiled them. It counts 22,17,619 such appellants among the 27,06,057 deleted, 82%, and finds Muslim names among 79.3% of them. The two sets of records cover 38,25,794 of the 59,59,458 electors sent to judicial officers in these constituencies, and The Wire counts 31,99,122 of them with Muslim names, which it says means that at least 53.7% of all those sent to adjudication had Muslim names even if none of the others did. In the seats under 10%, it finds Muslim names among about a third of the deleted electors who appealed and among 61.7% of the cleared electors the Commission appealed against.
court-65.response: The Wire says it has written to the office of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer and two Additional Chief Electoral Officers asking which officers filed the appeals, under what provision officers of that office can appeal against electors in constituencies they do not administer, whether registration officers were consulted, on what grounds and by what criteria electors were chosen, and whether each case was reviewed. It has also asked for the letter of 22 October that the Commission cites in its affidavit. It says the report will be updated when the office replies. The Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October (court-52), as the report quotes it, says officers of the Chief Electoral Officer's office filed the appeals as authorities under the Representation of the People Act and that the matters were not brought to the Commission. No reply from the Commission is reported.
court-65.headline: 9 in 10 Voters the Election Commission Wants Removed From Bengal’s Rolls Have Muslim Names

court-66.case: Writ petition by residents of Maharashtra to quash 14 orders of the Election Commission and the Chief Election Commissioner, Bombay High Court, Kolhapur Bench
court-66.claim: Residents of Maharashtra filed a writ petition before the Kolhapur Bench of the Bombay High Court through the advocate Asim Sarode asking it to quash 14 administrative orders passed by the Election Commission and the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, over the past ten months, Bar and Bench reported on 24 September. The petition relies on The Indian Express's report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected to these decisions on at least 14 occasions, and says the objections concerned voter registration, deletion and restoration of names, the electoral roll database, the functioning of registration officers and software. It argues that the Commission did not act in accordance with section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, and that the Chief Election Commissioner failed to discharge his duties faithfully, so that no protection can extend to his actions in office. It also challenges the changes made to Form 6 in July. It asks for the 14 orders to be quashed, for the revision in Maharashtra to be stayed, for every elector deleted in Maharashtra in the revision to be restored, for the Assembly elections due in the states where the revision was held to be postponed until rolls are prepared in accordance with law, and for a judicial committee headed by a retired High Court judge to inquire into the deletions and the blockages in the software. On 28 September a bench of Justices Sharmila Deshmukh and Neeraj Dhote declined Sarode's request to hear it that day or the next and listed it for 22 October, Bar and Bench reported. The bench asked what was urgent about it and what private right the petitioners held against the Commission, and Sarode replied that the petition was filed for voters who feel their rights are being infringed. No report of a hearing on 22 October or of any later order was found.
court-66.response: No reply from the Commission is reported. Pudhari and Lokmat report that the bench said the matter raised no urgent question of life or liberty and listed it in view of the court's workload. Sarode told a press conference reported by Saamana on 30 September that notice had been sent to the Commission before the hearing on 22 October.
