Searches on 9 November 2026 found no report of that hearing or of any later listing.
court-66.headline: Petition before Bombay High Court to quash orders by CEC Gyanesh Kumar, restore voters deleted in SIR

court-67.case: West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals of retired judges (court-18)
court-67.claim: The retired Calcutta High Court judge Biswajit Basu resigned on 7 November as head of one of West Bengal's 19 SIR appellate tribunals, citing personal reasons, and sent his resignation to the High Court's Chief Justice, Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge, The Indian Express, The Hindu, the Hindustan Times and The New Indian Express reported. He was one of the two tribunal heads hearing appeals from Murshidabad district, and The New Indian Express reports that he and Indrajit Chatterjee each had 11 of its 22 constituencies. The Times of India reports that Murshidabad had over 7.4 lakh appeals pending when the Commission reported to the Supreme Court in September. The reports count the resignations differently. The Hindu, the Hindustan Times, The New Indian Express and PTI, as The Times of India carried it, call him the fourth to resign, after the former Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court T.S. Sivagnanam and the retired judges Ranjit Kumar Bag and Indrajit Chatterjee, and The Hindu says Sivagnanam was the first, in May 2026. The Telegraph also calls him the fourth and does not name the others. The Indian Express calls him the second within a month in one report and the third in another, and The Times of India's Kolkata edition calls him the third in seven months. Those three reports and The Telegraph say Chatterjee stayed on after the Commission promised to deal with his complaints about the commute and its portal. The Indian Express reports, from sources, that Basu was unhappy with the tribunal's infrastructure and its login procedures, and its second report says the requirement of Aadhaar to log in to the Commission's portal was the last straw. The Times of India's Kolkata edition reports that the tribunals have not been examining appeals since 21 September, because the judges refused to log in to a new portal the Commission introduced. The Telegraph reports that no order has been uploaded to the portal since then, because the judges refused to share their Aadhaar details. Basu also chairs the state government's Commission on Institutional Corruption.
court-67.response: An official of the Commission told PTI that with both judges hearing Murshidabad's appeals stepping down within a month, the disposal of appeals from Murshidabad had effectively come to a standstill, as The Times of India carried it. The Trinamool Congress leader and lawyer Baiswanor Chatterjee asked what use the tribunal was when its judges had heard very few appeals, and the state BJP spokesperson Sayantan Basu said there was no reason to read anything into the resignation, since Justice Basu heads the inquiry commission probing corruption cases and was probably unable to spare the time, the Hindustan Times reported. No report says who will hear the appeals he was hearing.
court-67.headline: Bengal SIR tribunal sees another exit as retired judge Biswajit Basu resigns

court-68.case: Writ - A No. 18007 of 2026, a petition by five assistant teachers in Saharanpur against their deployment as booth level officers, Allahabad High Court
court-68.outlet: Allahabad High Court (judgment of 2.11.2026, as published by Bar and Bench)
court-68.claim: Justice Vinod Diwakar of the Allahabad High Court on 2 November dismissed a writ petition by five assistant teachers of junior and senior basic schools in Saharanpur district, who asked to be detached from their duties as booth level officers. The teachers argued that nothing in the terms of their service allows BLO duty to be given to them, and that it is contrary to Article 21-A of the Constitution and the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, because it takes teachers away from teaching. The court held that preparing and revising the roll is a statutory function under the Representation of the People Act, 1950, that under section 13CC of that Act state and local government staff employed on the roll are deemed to be on deputation to the Election Commission for that period, and that section 27 of the 2009 Act expressly permits teachers to be deployed for election duties, which include BLO duties. It found the argument on Article 21-A misconceived and said the teachers had not shown that their work as BLOs had harmed their teaching or the children's education. The judgment does not name the revision. The Hindustan Times and Bar and Bench report that the duties it covers include work in the SIR.
court-68.response: The judgment records that the court heard the State's standing counsel and gives no submission for the State or the Commission. No reply from the teachers was reported.
court-68.headline: Allahabad High Court holds that the RTE Act permits teachers to be deployed as booth level officers

court-69.case: Revision petition by the Banbhoolpura police against the Haldwani magistrate's order of 6 October to register an FIR over 28 Form 7s (form7-36), court of the First Additional Sessions Judge
court-69.claim: The First Additional Sessions Judge, Sujit Kumar, on 30 October rejected the Banbhoolpura police's application to stay a Haldwani magistrate's order of 6 October to register an FIR over Form 7s seeking the deletion of 28 electors (form7-36), Dainik Jagran and Live Hindustan reported on 11 November. The station house officer of Banbhoolpura had filed a revision petition against the order and asked for it to be stayed. The court held that the police are not a victim or an aggrieved party in the matter and that registering an FIR and investigating on information of a cognisable offence is their legal duty, Dainik Jagran reported. By the account of the complainant's advocate, Manish Kumar Pandey, the court also questioned why no FIR had been registered for about 24 days. The revision petition is listed for 7 December 2026, and with the stay refused the magistrate's order stands. The complainant, a resident of Indiranagar who says he is the BJP's booth level agent, alleges that an unknown person misused his identity and login to file the Form 7s online on 12 August 2026 against electors of part 134, that he learnt of it on 20 August, and that he neither filed them nor authorised anyone to. Live Hindustan reports that the order of 6 October was passed by the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Shubhangi Gupta. It also reports the complainant's account that he went to Delhi on 30 October and raised the case with more than 20 MPs and senior leaders of the INDIA bloc, among them Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, P. Chidambaram, Mahua Moitra and Mehbooba Mufti.
court-69.response: The Nainital Senior Superintendent of Police, Manjunath T.C., told Live Hindustan that the police were examining the legal aspects of the case. The complainant's advocate told Dainik Jagran that no FIR had yet been registered and called that a serious matter. Neither report gives the police's grounds for the revision petition. Live Hindustan says the allegations have not been confirmed and that the investigation of the forms, user IDs and login records on the Commission's portal could show who filed them. The police had told the magistrate that the complaint concerned SIR Form 7s and that the complainant could object before the assistant returning officer (form7-36).
court-69.headline: 28 मतदाताओं के नाम कटवाने के मामले में उत्तराखंड पुलिस की किरकिरी, अदालत ने ठुकराई अर्जी

court-70.case: Appeals against inclusion before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals (court-47)
court-70.claim: In 7,335 polling booths across 23 districts of West Bengal, every elector whom judicial officers examined and found eligible in the adjudication of logical discrepancies faces an appeal against inclusion before the SIR appellate tribunals, the Hindustan Times reported on 11 November from a report on the tribunals by the Civic Research Group, which it describes as a research collective based in Kolkata. The paper reports that these booths held 27,277 such electors, that by the group's analysis the appeals against 21,615 of them, 79%, were pending and those against 5,662 had been disposed of, and that every one of the state's 294 constituencies has at least one such booth. It reports from the group's report that the share of cleared electors facing an appeal is highest in Kalimpong at 71.4%, Purba Bardhaman at 59.7% and Darjeeling at 59.3%, and lowest in Dakshin Dinajpur at 39.3%, Cooch Behar at 39.4% and Nadia at 39.5%. The group compiled its statewide figures from the tribunals' appeal portal, the paper reports, and its published count is 16,08,175 appeals against inclusion, 15,26,933 of them pending and 81,242 disposed of. The group says the portal does not show the outcome of a disposed appeal.
court-70.response: The Commission declined to comment, the paper reported. A senior official of the Commission told it, on condition of anonymity, that the appeals were filed by officials of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer who had the authority to do so as per the Supreme Court, that this was a technicality, that an appeal against an elector does not mean the elector was ineligible to vote, and that the electors' names appeared in the supplementary lists, which meant they were eligible to vote in the Assembly election. The Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October cited a letter from the Chief Electoral Officer's office saying the office's officers had filed the appeals as authorities under the Representation of the People Act (court-57).
court-70.headline: In 7k WB booths, all cleared voters face EC exclusion plea

court-71.case: Writ petition over an EWS certificate withheld from a son because a parent was deleted in the revision, Calcutta High Court
court-71.claim: Justice Krishna Rao of the Calcutta High Court issued notice on a petition challenging the withholding of an Economically Weaker Section certificate from a candidate solely because his parent's name was deleted from the roll in the revision, and permitted an early hearing, LiveLaw reported on 12 November. The petitioner contends that the authorities are withholding the certificate on that ground alone, and the petitioner's counsel told the court that the son is eligible for it. The son had taken part in a government recruitment process and could go no further without the certificate, which is why the matter was urgent. The petition questions the link between a parent's deletion from the roll and the son's entitlement to the certificate.
court-71.response: LiveLaw gives no response from the State or from the authority that issues the certificate, and no date for the next hearing.
court-71.headline: Calcutta High Court Issues Notice On Plea Challenging Denial Of EWS Certificate To Son Over Parent's Deletion From SIR Rolls

court-72.case: Writ petition by a student refused a passport because his mother was deleted in the revision, Calcutta High Court
court-72.claim: Justice Krishna Rao of the Calcutta High Court directed the West Bengal government to file a report on a petition by a student who says he cannot obtain a passport because his mother's name was deleted from the roll in the revision, LiveLaw reported on 12 November. The student told the court that he had secured admission to a medical college in Bangladesh, that his own name is still on the roll and that he has voted. The court said the State had to be made a party and cautioned the petitioner against making the SIR tribunal a respondent, and he was directed to remove the tribunal from the respondents and add the State of West Bengal. The State is to file its report on the next date of hearing.
court-72.response: The passport authorities opposed the petition and said a police report should be obtained, LiveLaw reported. They said the mother's name had to be printed on the passport and asked how it could be printed when her name was no longer on the roll.
court-72.headline: Calcutta High Court Seeks State Response On Plea Against Passport Denial Over Mother's Name Being Deleted From SIR

court-73.case: Application by Karnataka's State Election Commission on the elections to the five city corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority, Supreme Court
court-73.claim: Karnataka's State Election Commission applied to the Supreme Court on 12 November for leave to hold the elections to the five city corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority on the final rolls published on 18 April 2026, and for time until 31 January 2027 to complete them on those earlier ward-wise rolls, Deccan Herald reported on 13 November. It also asked for leave to hold the elections to all panchayats and urban local bodies in the state on the Assembly rolls as they stood on 1 October 2025. The Supreme Court had directed on 17 July that the five corporation elections be completed by 31 December 2026. The State Election Commission told the Court that unforeseen delays in the final publication of the Assembly rolls on 27 October, and the Election Commission's not supplying complete and authenticated roll data since then, had disrupted its schedule. It said it needs the full data, with the additions, deletions, transpositions and corrections, to divide the rolls by ward and to map, verify and publish them. Deccan Herald reports that the data had still not been supplied when the application was filed. It estimated that if it had to wait for the new rolls it would need at least two months after receiving the data to prepare the ward rolls and another month to hold the elections. It said it had already prepared and published rolls for the five corporations from the data of 1 October 2025 that the Election Commission had supplied, and had printed and distributed state voter identity cards on that basis. On 5 November it had told the five corporations to prepare ward rolls from the final rolls of 27 October (protest-66).
court-73.response: Deccan Herald gives no response from the Election Commission or from the state government, and no date on which the Court will hear the application.
court-73.headline: GBA polls: Karnataka SEC seeks Supreme Court nod to use pre-SIR rolls

court-74.case: Writ petition by an Army aspirant refused a domicile certificate because his mother was deleted in the revision, Calcutta High Court
court-74.claim: Justice Krishna Rao of the Calcutta High Court agreed to hear a petition by an Indian Army aspirant who asks for a domicile certificate so that he can take part in the second phase of the Army's recruitment process, LiveLaw reported on 13 November. The petitioner says the authorities refused him the certificate because his mother's name was deleted from the roll in the revision. He told the court that his father's name is still on the roll after the revision, and that he has only just turned 21 and his own name has not yet been registered in the revision. Without the certificate he cannot go further in the recruitment process. The court listed the matter for hearing.
court-74.response: LiveLaw gives no response from the State or from the authority that issues domicile certificates, and no date for the hearing.
court-74.headline: Indian Army Aspirant Moves Calcutta High Court After Denial Of Domicile Certificate Over Deletion Of Mother's Name In SIR

court-75.case: Letters of the Chief Electoral Officer's office, West Bengal, to the Registrar General of the Calcutta High Court on adjudication cases that judicial officers had not decided or not e-signed (court-59)
court-75.claim: The office of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer told the Registrar General of the Calcutta High Court in memos dated 12 October and 29 October 2026 that judicial officers had not decided 815 adjudication cases and had decided 5,004 more without e-signing them, The Wire reported on 13 November. The two figures add to 5,819, which is the 'around 6,000' of The Wire's headline. The Wire publishes the memo of 12 October, No. 9806-Home (Elec) from the Additional Chief Electoral Officer. It says the Commission's IT team wrote on 6 August that the logins of the judicial officers of the constituencies concerned had been reactivated, and it asks the Registrar General to have those officers e-sign the decided cases and decide the rest at the earliest. It refers to an earlier memo of 7 August. The Wire reports that the memo of 29 October gives the same two figures, and that the office asked district election officers the same day to report on these cases by 3 November, before the integrated draft roll of the special summary revision due on 23 November. The Wire says the Commission's ECINET report 'Individuals Under Adjudication' of 9 April, which it has seen, records 22,163 cases that judges had not decided when the judicial review ended and 83,504 that they had decided and not signed, 44,027 of them found eligible. It reports that 12,337 of the undecided cases were in Murshidabad, 5,194 in Purba Bardhaman and 3,374 in South 24 Parganas, across 67 constituencies, with 3,183 in Farakka. The Wire's own count, from the rolls of 304 polling stations in 11 of Murshidabad's 22 constituencies, is 29,347 electors still marked under adjudication, which it says is five times the number the Chief Electoral Officer's office gives for the whole state. In three polling stations of Mahadebnagar gram panchayat in Farakka, whose roll as revised up to 6 April it has seen, it counts 1,914, and booth level officers told it that the judicial review there never took place. The Wire says an elector whose case was never decided has no order to take to the appellate tribunals and was not able to vote in April.
court-75.response: The Wire says it asked the Chief Electoral Officer on 5 November why 22,163 cases had not been decided by the time the roll was frozen, when and by whom they were decided while the judicial officers' logins were inactive, and how many of those electors were found eligible, and that it will update the report on a reply. It gives no response from the Chief Electoral Officer's office, the Election Commission or the High Court.
court-75.headline: Election Commission Says Around 6,000 Voters in Bengal Are Still ‘Under Adjudication’. In Just 22 Seats, the Real Number is Almost 30,000

court-76.case: W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026, the petition on the Commission's functioning (court-52, court-53), in which LiveLaw reports the affidavit was filed, and the petition on Delhi's revision, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026 (court-54, court-60, court-61), with which The Hindu reports it, Supreme Court
court-76.claim: The Election Commission filed a supplementary affidavit in the Supreme Court on 14 November 2026, The Hindu reported. LiveLaw reports that Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu filed it on behalf of the Commission in the writ petition that leads the batch on the Commission's functioning, W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026 (court-52, court-53). The interrogatories that INDIA bloc leaders asked the Court on 16 November for leave to serve also describe it as sworn by Yeturu (court-78). The Indian Express describes it as a joint affidavit of the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, and the Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. The Hindu gives no case number and reports the affidavit together with the concerns about Form 6 raised by the petitioners in the case on Delhi's revision, in which Anjali Bhardwaj is a petitioner (court-54, court-60, court-61). The affidavit says the Commission took note of the Court's suggestion at the hearing of 28 October that it reach out to electors left off as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, and that by a communication of 6 November it directed the Chief Electoral Officers of the states and union territories where the revision is under way, which LiveLaw lists as Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland, to let electors left off the draft roll submit the enumeration form (Annexure A) to the Electoral Registration Officer or Assistant Electoral Registration Officer for their current ordinary residence. An elector who has not shifted may submit the signed form with an Annexure B statement giving the reason it was not submitted earlier, in person or through family members, to the Electoral Registration Officer, the Assistant Electoral Registration Officer or the booth level officer, and that an option to submit it online with e-sign will be available on ECINET. An elector who has shifted within the state does not need Form 8 and may submit the enumeration form with an Annexure C statement giving the new address and Assembly constituency, and proof of address, to the Electoral Registration Officer or Assistant Electoral Registration Officer of the new constituency. The affidavit says booth-wise lists of electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate are to be displayed afresh with the probable reasons why they were not included, and that Electoral Registration Officers are to process the enumeration forms of these electors under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 and re-assign the same EPIC number to them. It says a previously enrolled elector who has already filed Form 6 need not submit the enumeration form again, and that such applications will be processed under the clarification of 3 November (court-60). It repeats that clarification, that no prosecution will be launched against anyone for filing Form 6 merely because the applicant was enrolled before the revision and was not in the draft roll, provided the applicant is not enrolled in any other Parliamentary or Assembly constituency and the declaration is otherwise in accordance with law. ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, also reported the affidavit and says the Chief Electoral Officers have been asked to give the clarification wide publicity, in local languages as well. The affidavit says a mechanism has been directed to ensure that no eligible elector is deprived of the chance to be included in the final roll, with due care to avoid duplicate enrolment. It also says that after a new Deputy Election Commissioner joined on 2 November, a work order of 4 November gave oversight of the Commission's IT division to a Senior Deputy Election Commissioner, that the Director General (IT) puts the division's files to the Commission through that officer, and that the IT division has always been under the supervision of a Deputy Election Commissioner. The Times of India also reported the affidavit, from PTI. The batch on the Commission's functioning was tentatively listed for 17 November (court-53), and the Delhi case is listed for 19 November (court-61).
court-76.response: The affidavit is the Commission's own account of what it has done since the hearing of 28 October (court-54). The Indian Express and ThePrint quote it as saying it 'remains committed to its constitutional duty of ensuring the purity of the election process' and that problems 'have been and will be' arising from time to time. None of the five reports gives a response from the petitioners or a hearing on the affidavit.
court-76.headline: ‘Alive’ to voters’ need to find their names on the electoral roll, ECI assures Supreme Court

court-77.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals against electors cleared by judicial officers (court-47, court-57, court-58)
court-77.claim: Jawhar Sircar, a retired IAS officer, former Rajya Sabha member and former Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal, wrote to the state's Chief Electoral Officer, Neelam Meena, on 13 November 2026 asking who ordered the appeals filed before the appellate tribunals against 16,10,311 electors whom judicial officers had found eligible, and on what authority, The Wire reported on 14 November from the letter, which was shared with it. The letter says it appears that the Chief Electoral Officer's office filed these appeals in April 2026 although each of these electors had been checked and included in the rolls by judicial officers. It cites the Commission's counter affidavit in the Supreme Court in October (court-52), which, as The Wire gives it, says in paragraph 63 that officers of the Chief Electoral Officer's office filed the appeals and in paragraph 60 that these electors' documents are on the portal with a favourable order of the judicial officer. Sircar asks how more than 12 lakh appeals carrying a single batch code for 5 April could have been filed in one day, what part the Commission's IT division played, and whether the processing of names for deletion was decided by the Commission's IT system. He asks how appeals against 599 electors in Hemtabad, Uttar Dinajpur, could carry the batch code of 5 April when the supplementary list that cleared them was published on 6 April, a finding The Wire first reported (court-58). He also asks whether the special drive for left-out electors is open to everyone missing from the roll before the revision or only to those on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors. He writes that the Commission's letter of 1 October, which told booth level officers to compare the current roll with the roll before the revision, would cover 27.16 lakh electors deleted by judicial officers and 5.46 lakh deleted through Form 7. The Commission's letter and the Chief Electoral Officer's press note of 7 October both say that anyone whose name has been deleted can apply for enrolment at any time, and he asks whether that includes the roughly 22 lakh electors who have appealed to the tribunals, and whether an Electoral Registration Officer can enrol an elector deleted by judicial officers whose appeal is pending. He writes that the Chief Electoral Officer had neither acknowledged nor answered his first letter, of 22 October, in three weeks.
court-77.response: The Wire says it has written to the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer's office several times in recent weeks about the appeals, the electors still under adjudication and the special drive, and will update the report on a reply. It reports that the Commission has told the Supreme Court that the appeals were filed by officers of the Chief Electoral Officer's office 'in their capacity as authorities under the RP Act', with authority under the Court's orders, and that 'these matters were not brought to the commission', and that the Commission has not named the officers or given the grounds of the appeals.
court-77.headline: 'Who Ordered 16 Lakh Appeals Against Voters Cleared by Judges?' Jawhar Sircar Asks West Bengal CEO

court-78.case: The batch of petitions on the Commission's functioning, item 26 before the bench of the Chief Justice in the Supreme Court's cause list of 17 November 2026, led by W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026, with the INDIA bloc leaders' petition, W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026, as item 26.5 (court-43, court-52, court-53)
court-78.claim: INDIA bloc leaders asked the Supreme Court on 16 November 2026 for permission to put 48 written questions, known as interrogatories, to the Election Commission, Business Standard reported. The Congress announced the application in a post on X and published with it 17 pages of the filing, headed Annexure A-1, Interrogatories on behalf of the Petitioners. The filing names who is to answer each question on affidavit. They are Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu, whom it describes as the deponent of the Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October (court-52) and of its supplementary affidavit of 14 November (court-76), the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, and the Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, who are to answer from their own knowledge, including their own approval, participation, objection, dissent or concurrence, and the Commission's Director General (IT). Where a question is put to more than one person, each is to answer it on a separate affidavit. The questions are grouped in ten parts. They ask on what date and by what means each of the three Commissioners approved the filing of the counter affidavit, and in which file and on what date the Commission took the decision, recited in its order of 24 June 2025, to begin the revision in the entire country. They ask whether the order of the Commission's first appellate authority in an RTI appeal, which said the Commission had so far taken no decision on a revision across the country in 2025, was correct when it was made. They ask on how many occasions between 19 February 2025 and 26 October 2026 Sandhu or Joshi recorded in writing an objection, dissent or reservation on the revision, ECINET, Form 6 or the filing of appeals, and whether any decision on the revision was taken by majority under Section 18(2) of the 2023 Act. Other parts concern the office order of 28 July 2026 and the two Election Commissioners' joint direction of 30 July, the appeals filed in West Bengal against electors included by judicial officers, the accounts that can add, delete, modify or restore entries in the electoral roll database and whether ECINET's audit trail since 24 June 2025 is intact, the 97 Goa electors, the declaration added to the online Form 6, objections in Form 7, the office order of 4 November and the letters of 3 and 6 November annexed to the supplementary affidavit, and whether approvals given by electronic means were sought or conveyed by e-mail, WhatsApp or another messaging application. The Congress said in its post that the Commission's affidavit had not answered a single question raised on what the party calls Vote Chori. Bar and Bench reported that Rahul Gandhi and ten other opposition leaders moved the application. It names the eleven as the petitioners who filed the petition in October. They are Rahul Gandhi, Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge, Saugata Roy of the Trinamool Congress, Samajwadi Party President Akhilesh Yadav, Tejashwi Prasad Yadav of the Rashtriya Janata Dal, Sanjay Raut of the Shiv Sena (UBT), M.A. Baby of the CPI(M), D. Raja of the CPI, Mahua Majhi of the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha, Supriya Sule of the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) and Mohammed Basheer of the IUML. PTI, in The Tribune, reported that the application was filed in Rahul Gandhi's pending petition. Bar and Bench reported that the application seeks permission under Order V Rule 1, Order XXXVIII Rule 11(9) and Order LV Rule 6 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013 to serve the interrogatories. It reported that the petitioners rely on the Constitution Bench judgment in Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India for the point that the Court may require officials to answer specific questions where facts central to a constitutional challenge lie within the exclusive knowledge of an authority administering a technological system. It reported that the application asks that, if the Commission claims privilege over any official record, it be directed to state the specific grounds for each record so that the Court can decide the claim. It also reported that the interrogatories seek state-wise data on electors dropped from the draft and final rolls. The Supreme Court's cause list for 17 November 2026 lists the batch, led by W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026, as item 26 before the bench of the Chief Justice, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana, with W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026, Rahul Gandhi and others against the Election Commission of India and others, as item 26.5.
court-78.response: The interrogatories can be served only if the Court allows the application, and no order on it had been reported. The Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October said that the three SIR orders were unanimous decisions of the Commission and that a suggestion, observation or query by a member while a file moves is not a decision of the Commission (court-52). No reply by the Commission to the application was reported.
court-78.headline: INDIA bloc seeks SC nod to question EC members over SIR, submits 48 queries

court-79.case: Rahul Gandhi v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026, item 26.5 in the batch led by W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026, Supreme Court (court-42, court-43, court-52, court-78)
court-79.claim: Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders have told the Supreme Court in a rejoinder to the Election Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October (court-52) that the Commission gave no proof of its claim that the SIR was a unanimous decision of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, The Wire reported on 16 November 2026. The rejoinder says the counter affidavit gives no particulars or dates of that approval, and that the Court should not take into account "a bare assertion of unanimous decision of the Election Commissioners without perusal of the relevant recorded files". It says the affidavit does not explain when the decision to hold the revision across the country was taken, where it was recorded, or how the Commission's RTI replies that no such decision had been taken are to be reconciled with its order of 24 June 2025. It says the affidavit was signed by a Deputy Election Commissioner on behalf of the three members, who are all senior to him, and that a general statement by an administrative officer cannot take the place of the primary records or of the members' own explanation. It says that Sandhu and Joshi writing to the Cabinet Secretary is "itself inconsistent with the picture of unanimous functioning" that the Commission presents. On Form 6 it says that calling the declaration a separate component does not change the fact that an applicant using the online Form 6 process "was required to encounter and complete the additional declaration as part of that process". The Wire reports that the petitioners say 97 electors in Goa were deleted and could not be added back because local electoral officials could not get into the software to enrol them again, and that the Commission's affidavit said 88 were added back through Form 6 applications. Bar and Bench reported the same affidavit as saying 88 of the 97 had since applied through Form 6 (court-52). The rejoinder says the affidavit "does not deny that the software lacked a facility to restore these electors". It says the office order of 1997 on which the Commission relies does not cover the design of the roll software, changes to statutory forms or application procedures, or the bringing of litigation or appeals. On the appeals filed by officers of the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer against electors the tribunals had cleared, it says that if they were acts of the Commission, "the respondents must disclose the decision of the commission authorising the same, together with the relevant approval and delegation records". The Hindu reported the same day that Rahul Gandhi had told the Court that the Commission produced no proof that the SIR was a unanimous decision of the three members, and that the Commission's affidavit of 26 October answered a petition by INDIA bloc leaders led by him. The Wire gives the hearing as 17 November before a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant, and the Supreme Court's cause list for that day lists the petition as item 26.5 (court-78).
court-79.response: These are the petitioners' submissions in a rejoinder, as The Wire reports them. The Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October said that the three SIR orders were unanimous decisions of the Commission, that Form 6 has not been amended and the SIR declaration is a separate document, and that the West Bengal appeals were filed by officers of the state Chief Electoral Officer under the Court's orders and were not placed before the Commission (court-52). No reply by the Commission to the rejoinder was reported, and the Court had made no finding on any of these points.
court-79.headline: No Material Evidence to Show SIR Was EC’s ‘Unanimous’ Decision, Rahul Gandhi Tells Supreme Court

court-80.case: The batch of petitions on the Commission's functioning, item 26 before the bench of the Chief Justice on 17 November 2026, led by W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026, with Rahul Gandhi v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026, as item 26.5, and the application in it for leave to serve 48 interrogatories (court-53, court-78, court-79)
court-80.claim: A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana said on 17 November 2026 that the matter will be heard on 9 December after the Election Commission files its objections to the application by Rahul Gandhi and ten other opposition leaders for leave to serve 48 interrogatories on the Commission (court-78), Bar and Bench reported. The Chief Justice told the Commission's counsel that it may file its reply and raise its objections, and said the Court would examine the interrogatories and then decide. Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal appeared for Rahul Gandhi. The Indian Express reported in its live coverage that the Court adjourned the hearing of the batch of petitions on the Commission's functioning and that the petitions will now be taken up on 9 December. Amar Ujala reported that the hearing on the petitions of Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders was put off to 9 December. No order on the application was reported.
court-80.response: Senior Advocate Harish Salve, for the Commission, said the Commission had serious reservations about the application, Bar and Bench reported, and told the Court "We have something to say about that. There is very serious prejudice." The Commission's written objections had not been reported filed.
court-80.headline: Rahul Gandhi's plea to serve 48 interrogatories on ECI: Supreme Court to decide after considering ECI's objections

court-81.case: A writ petition by Ali Mehdi, the Congress candidate for Mustafabad in the 2025 Assembly election, on Form 7 objections in Mustafabad, filed in the Supreme Court on 16 November 2026 (form7-58, form7-60, form7-62, form7-67)
court-81.claim: Ali Mehdi, a Congress leader and the party's candidate for Mustafabad in the 2025 Delhi Assembly election, approached the Supreme Court on Monday, 16 November 2026, alleging that a "substantial" number of the Form 7 applications seeking the deletion of electors in Mustafabad, Assembly constituency 69, during Delhi's revision are what The Hindu calls ghost Form 7s, the paper reported on 17 November. The summary The Hindu shows with the report says the petition cites living electors recorded as dead and fabricated objections, and that it says persons declared dead were alive and persons said to have shifted were found at home.
court-81.response: The report is for subscribers, and only the headline, the summary and the opening paragraph The Hindu shows free are used. They give no hearing date, order or reply from the Election Commission. The North East Delhi District Election Officer's office had said on 31 October that every elector against whom a Form 7 had been filed in Mustafabad would be visited before any name is deleted (form7-58), and the Electoral Registration Officer had sought an FIR against one booth level agent on 6 November (form7-62).
court-81.headline: Plea in SC says ghost Form 7s haunt Mustafabad constituency during Delhi SIR

court-82.case: Electors in West Bengal whose cases are still under adjudication after the judicial review the Supreme Court ordered, and the Chief Electoral Officer's letters on the judicial officers' logins (court-59, court-75)
court-82.claim: Electors in West Bengal whose eligibility went before judicial officers and is still marked under adjudication have not reached the appellate tribunals, The Indian Express reported on 17 November 2026. The paper puts their number, from unnamed sources, at over 25,000 in Murshidabad, Malda, Nadia and Howrah, and says poll officials admitted they were not sure of the total. The state's Additional Chief Electoral Officer wrote to district election officers on 29 October about reactivating the login IDs of judicial officers to dispose of cases in which the decision and the e-signing were pending, and asked for the status of disposal by 3 November. The paper reports that at polling station 44, in ward 21 of the Samserganj constituency in Murshidabad, 590 of the 949 electors left on the roll after the names marked dead and displaced were removed, 62%, are still under adjudication. The booth level officer of part 192 in Farakka told the paper that 799 of the 1,372 electors in his part are still under adjudication, and that the assistant electoral registration officer and other officials told the booth level officers they were helpless and to go to court. An elector in Dhulian told the paper that he would have appealed to the tribunals had his name been deleted, that he can neither appeal nor vote, and that his family's last hearing was on 30 January, at the Dhulian Municipality office. The paper says the others under adjudication have been waiting for word since December 2025 or January. Another elector in Dhulian, a primary schoolteacher who was on poll duty in the Assembly election, said she could not vote in it.
court-82.response: A senior official in the Chief Electoral Officer's office, whom the paper does not name, said the office had informed the Calcutta High Court and that the Chief Electoral Officer had informed the Election Commission. The Additional Chief Electoral Officer, Arindam Niyogi, said only the court could decide the cases. The paper could not reach the Chief Electoral Officer, Neelam Meena. Krishanu Mitra of the Trinamool Congress blamed the Union Government, Sujan Chakraborty of the CPI(M) said the government now decides through the Commission who will vote, Soumya Aich Roy of the Congress said the Commission had carried out targeted exclusion, and Ritesh Tiwary, a BJP MLA, said it was for the Commission to answer.
court-82.headline: ‘Can’t appeal, can’t vote’: The forgotten voters of Bengal SIR

court-83.case: Network of Women in Media, India v. Union of India and others, W.P.(C) No. 1361 of 2026, and connected petitions on the police's treatment of journalists covering the protests against the Chief Election Commissioner in October, Supreme Court (court-36, court-62)
court-83.claim: The Delhi Police told the Supreme Court in a counter-affidavit that the Court's direction of 11 October protecting journalists covering the protests against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, does not extend to reel-makers and social media influencers, LiveLaw and Bar and Bench reported. The affidavit answers petitions by the Network of Women in Media, India, the Free Speech Collective, the Delhi Union of Journalists and the Kerala Union of Working Journalists on the police's treatment of journalists at the protests. LiveLaw reports that the order of 11 October recorded the Solicitor General's assurance that lawyers, journalists and other professionals would not be hindered in their professional duties. The police said the direction protects journalists in the discharge of their duties and was not meant to exempt reel-makers, influencers or unruly elements from the general law or from lawful police directions at the site of a prohibited assembly, and that whether reel-makers can be treated as journalists is yet to be determined. Bar and Bench reports that the affidavit accepts that independent media persons, freelancers and people reporting on YouTube or other digital platforms may gather and publish news without accreditation or a press card, and says they remain subject to the general law and to lawful police directions. On the complaints of sexual harassment by a police officer at the protest near Jantar Mantar on 3 October, Bar and Bench reports the affidavit as saying that two of the three journalists who complained did not wish to pursue their complaints, that the third did not join the inquiry, that CCTV footage showed no act of sexual harassment, and that the three complaints have been filed and the matter closed. LiveLaw reports the affidavit as saying that four complaints were received from women journalists after the protests of 3 October and sent to the Crime Branch, and that the CCTV footage did not corroborate the specific allegations. The police answered other journalists' allegations of obstruction and detention one by one, denied seizing any journalist's equipment and asked the Court to dismiss the petitions, Bar and Bench reported. LiveLaw reports the affidavit as saying that any journalist removed from a protest site by mistake was released as soon as their credentials were verified.
court-83.response: The affidavit is the police's reply to the petitions. LiveLaw reports that the police defended their advisory of 5 October asking journalists covering protests to carry an identity card from their organisation or an accreditation card, and said that the absence of accreditation would not by itself stop a journalist being identified. No reply from the petitioners and no hearing date were reported.
court-83.headline: Reel Makers Not Entitled To Journalistic Protection During Protests, Delhi Police To Supreme Court

court-84.case: An advocate's application under section 175(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita for an FIR against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, and others, magistrate's court, Delhi
court-84.claim: The Delhi Police submitted an action taken report to a magistrate's court on 17 November 2026 on an advocate's application for an FIR against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, and others, and asked for more time to complete its inquiry, The New Indian Express and Dainik Jagran reported. The advocate had applied under section 175(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, under which a magistrate can order an investigation, and the magistrate had asked the police for the report. The report says the complaint relates to allegations of deliberate voter suppression, manipulation and deletion of names from the electoral rolls and offences by officials of the Election Commission and others, that the allegations are extensive and need detailed examination of records and of the role of the persons concerned, and that the inquiry could not be conducted because of heavy law and order duty. The application says that the advocate gave a written complaint at the Parliament Street police station on 23 September alleging deliberate voter suppression, fraud, criminal conspiracy, misappropriation of funds and criminal breach of trust by public servants, that its immediate trigger was a newspaper report that two Election Commissioners had objected on record at least 14 times in 10 months to six decisions taken and orders issued without their knowledge, and that the police took no action on it.
court-84.response: The reports give no response from the Commission or the Chief Election Commissioner. None of them names the court or the magistrate or gives the next date.
court-84.headline: Delhi Police seeks more time to probe voter suppression allegations against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

court-85.case: Ali Mehdi v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 1493 of 2026, the petition on Form 7 objections in Mustafabad, Supreme Court (court-81, form7-58, form7-60, form7-62, form7-67)
court-85.claim: The bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana disposed of the petition by Ali Mehdi, the Congress candidate for Mustafabad in 2025, on Form 7 objections in Mustafabad (court-81) on 19 November 2026, LiveLaw and Bar and Bench reported. The bench directed the Election Commission and Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer to verify the petitioner's allegations and take the necessary remedial measures strictly in accordance with law, and expressed no opinion on the merits. The petition, citing newspaper reports, said that 28 electors against whom deletion applications had been filed were found living at their addresses, and counsel for the petitioner told the Court that the authorities had accepted that 36 of the 37 objections filed in the name of one booth level agent were false (form7-62). He said the police had not registered an FIR on the petitioner's complaint, and asked that no name be deleted on a Form 7 without the prescribed notices to the objector and to the elector. The bench said that the Commission's power over a booth level agent, who is an agent of a political party, goes no further than blacklisting one who makes a fraudulent application. LiveLaw gives that remark to Justice Bagchi and Bar and Bench to the Chief Justice. LiveLaw reports that Justice Bagchi told the petitioner to approach the magistrate for an FIR. Bar and Bench reports the Chief Justice as saying that the complaint should name the booth level agents concerned so that remedial and, if necessary, disciplinary steps can be taken, and the bench as saying that the petitioner can make a representation to the Commission.
court-85.response: The reports give no submission by the Commission or the Chief Electoral Officer at the hearing. The North East Delhi District Election Officer's office had said on 31 October that every elector against whom a Form 7 had been filed in Mustafabad would be visited before any name is deleted (form7-58), and the Electoral Registration Officer had sought an FIR against one booth level agent on 6 November (form7-62).
court-85.headline: Delhi SIR : Supreme Court Asks ECI To Verify Complaint Of False Form 7s Filed To Delete Mustafabad Voters

court-86.case: Anjali Bhardwaj and another v. Election Commission of India and others, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, an interlocutory application by the petitioners on Delhi's revision, Supreme Court (court-54, court-60, court-61, form7-61)
court-86.claim: Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, the petitioners in the Supreme Court case on Delhi's revision (court-54, court-61), have filed an interlocutory application asking the Court to extend the timeline of Delhi's revision and to direct the Election Commission to carry out its instructions of 6 November on electors in the ASDD list, those marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, LiveLaw, The Tribune and The New Indian Express reported on 18 November 2026. The application says 47,56,722 electors in Delhi were placed in that list. It says Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer continues to direct these electors to Form 6, that he has issued no standard operating procedure or instructions to registration officers and booth level officers for the new mechanism, and that the Commission has announced no revised timeline. It asks the Court to direct the Commission to implement the instructions of 6 November and file a compliance report, to let every elector in Delhi's ASDD list submit an enumeration form and have the earlier EPIC number restored whether or not the elector has already filed Form 6, and to publish constituency-wise and consolidated figures of these electors who have submitted enumeration forms and of those restored to the roll. On Form 7, the application cites The Hindu's report that 787 objections seeking the deletion of Muslim electors in Mustafabad were filed in the names of 20 booth level agents of the BJP, at least 16 of whom denied filing or authorising them (form7-60). It asks for an impartial inquiry into the use of Form 7 in Mustafabad and other areas, for FIRs wherever cognisable offences such as forgery, criminal impersonation and identity fraud are disclosed, and for action under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 against anyone found to have knowingly made a false declaration. It also asks for an audit of every Form 7 filed in Delhi during the revision to check whether the objectors named authorised and signed them, for every Form 7 to be disclosed publicly, for periodic audits, physical verification of objections and checks on the identity of objectors, and for a booth level agent who files a Form 7 to declare that status, to be shown in the Form 10 disclosures.
court-86.response: The reports give no reply from the Commission or the Chief Electoral Officer and no date on which the application will be heard. The Tribune gives Delhi's schedule as revised on 29 October: claims and objections until 25 November, decisions by 15 December and the final roll on 22 December. The petition was listed for admission on 19 November with two applications (list-06). At that listing the bench posted it to 2 December and asked the Commission for the number of enumeration forms and of Form 6, Form 7 and Form 8 applications (court-89). The reports of that hearing do not give this application's number or say whether the bench passed an order on it.
court-86.headline: Delhi SIR : Petitioners Cite Report On Form 7 Misuse, Seek Supreme Court Directions

court-87.case: Pleas by the Government of Karnataka and Karnataka's State Election Commission on the elections to the five city corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority, Supreme Court (court-73)
court-87.claim: The Government of Karnataka and the State Election Commission have asked the Supreme Court to allow the elections to the five city corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority to be held on the ward-wise rolls published on 18 April 2026, before the Election Commission's revision of the rolls in the state, The Indian Express reported on 19 November 2026 (court-73). The state government's plea says that by the final roll the Election Commission published on 27 October the electorate of Bengaluru fell from about 1.03 crore to 59.08 lakh, and calls this a mass deletion of over 43 lakh names in the Greater Bengaluru area. The State Election Commission told the Court that the rolls of 18 April list 88,95,361 electors in the five corporations, and that the Election Commission's final rolls for the 28 Assembly constituencies in Bengaluru district list 59,08,151 electors with the rural areas and 51,87,575 without them. It said the Election Commission had not shared the authenticated database of the final roll more than three weeks after its publication, and that it would need two months from receiving the data to prepare ward-wise rolls. It said that if it may use the rolls of 18 April it will complete the elections on or before 31 January 2027, and the state has asked for the Court's deadline of 31 December 2026 to be extended to that date. The State Election Commission had written to the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, on 19 September that if work began only after the final publication on 27 October it would be extremely difficult to prepare the rolls and hold the elections within December 2026.
court-87.response: The report gives no reply from the Election Commission and no date of hearing. The Times of India reported on 18 November that the Greater Bengaluru Authority had announced the schedule of the special summary revision, with the draft roll on 1 December, claims and objections until 31 December and the final roll on 20 January 2027, and that the State Election Commission has said the revision will not affect the schedule of the corporation elections.
court-87.headline: Allow Bengaluru civic polls on old rolls: Karnataka, State Election Commission to Supreme Court

court-88.case: Kirana Committee Delhi and another v. Union of India and others, W.P.(C) No. 1395 of 2026, the traders' petition on the protests against the Chief Election Commissioner and on Ramlila Maidan as a protest site, Supreme Court (protest-47, court-35, court-36)
court-88.claim: The bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana issued notice on 18 November 2026 to the Cockroach Janta Party, the Congress, the Aam Aadmi Party and the All India Students' Association on a petition by two traders' associations, the Kirana Committee Delhi and the Delhi Iron and Hardware Merchant Association, which say that the protests these organisations held in Delhi in October against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, hurt their business, LiveLaw reported. Hindustan Times reports that the bench also sought replies from the Centre and the Delhi government. On 3 November the Court had asked whether the organisers of the protests had been made parties, and the associations then added them. The petition was first raised in the Court on 16 October (protest-47). Their counsel, Mukul Rohatgi, objected to the designation of Ramlila Maidan as a protest venue. Hindustan Times reports that the petition asks for the Delhi Police's order of 11 October designating Ramlila Maidan as a protest site to be quashed and for a fresh, reasoned assessment. It puts Delhi's daily business at about Rs 500 crore to Rs 600 crore, of which it says about Rs 250 crore was at risk each day in the peak season from October 2026 to January 2027. The associations say they are not asking for a ban on peaceful protests. They ask for a framework for the location, duration and scale of demonstrations and for continued access to markets, homes, hospitals and public transport. The bench said the petition can be heard with MA Baby v. Union of India and the connected petitions on the restrictions imposed during the protests (court-35), which are tentatively listed on 27 November, and that it will take the contempt petitions against the police and other authorities separately on another day (court-36).
court-88.response: The Solicitor General, Tushar Mehta, told the Court that the petition should be heard with the petitions on the police action during the protests, because the traders' rights and the right to protest are contesting rights, Hindustan Times reported. No reply from the parties and organisations named had been reported.
court-88.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice To CJP, Congress, AAP & AISA On Delhi Traders' Plea Against Protests

court-89.case: Anjali Bhardwaj and another v. Election Commission of India and others, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, the petition on Delhi's revision, Supreme Court (court-54, court-61, court-86)
court-89.claim: The bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana heard Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri's petition on Delhi's revision on 19 November 2026 and posted it to 2 December, Hindustan Times, The Times of India and The Indian Express reported. The bench asked the Election Commission's counsel, Dama Seshadri Naidu, to say how many enumeration forms had been filled and how many Form 6, Form 7 and Form 8 applications had been made, and said that on the cut-off date it would consider whether the facility to use these forms had been provided, Hindustan Times reported. The Times of India reports that the figures asked for are of the enumeration forms and the Forms 6 and 8 received and approved between 30 October and 30 November, and The Hindu, in the standfirst of its report, that the Court asked for the number of applications received for the inclusion, deletion and correction of names. The reports name different deadlines. Hindustan Times says the petition seeks to extend 25 November, the last date for claims and objections in Delhi. The Times of India says the Court may extend 30 November, and the headline of The Hindu's report gives 30 November as the deadline for electors to be included again. Under the Commission's letter of 17 November, as Hindustan Times reported it, 30 November is also the last day for handing out and collecting the enumeration forms of electors left off the draft roll as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate. Prashant Bhushan, for the petitioners, said the Commission had decided on 6 November that these electors could fill enumeration forms, that no standard operating procedure followed, that the forms were not available until 17 November and that the Commission allowed them to be downloaded online on 19 November, Hindustan Times reported. The Indian Express reports him saying that the Court's earlier direction to let these electors submit forms had not been carried out on the ground, that the Court had called the use of Form 6 for them an error, and that they should use the enumeration form or Form 8. The bench told the petitioners that the priority now was to include every eligible elector and that the issues they raised would be decided when the time came, The Times of India reported. It said that what mattered was whether its orders reached the ground so that people could use the facility, Hindustan Times reported.
court-89.response: Naidu said he would provide the figures, Hindustan Times reported. No report gives an order of the Court or a reply by the Commission on the deadline. The Commission's letter of 6 November to the Chief Electoral Officers of seven states, Delhi among them, on enumeration forms for these electors is on the process page.
court-89.headline: Supreme Court seeks Delhi SIR progress data to decide on deadline extension

court-90.case: West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals of retired judges (court-18, court-67)
court-90.claim: Twelve housekeeping staff of West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals at Joka in Kolkata went on strike on 19 November because their salaries had not been paid, The Times of India reported. It was the second time in November that they stopped work. They have worked for four months and been paid for one, and a source told the paper that the current staff have worked since July and were paid only for September, before Durga Puja. Their monthly salary is Rs 14,500, a source said. The agency that employs them told them that the state had not paid it. The paper reports from sources in the tribunals that the drivers of the cars that carry the judges have also not been paid, because the agencies that supply the cars have received nothing, and that several drivers have left. Each judge's car, a Toyota Innova, was hired for Rs 1,20,000 a month, and the payments have not been made. The four buses that bring secretarial and office staff from Howrah, Sealdah, Baruipur and Diamond Harbour have not been paid for either. A source said that the state government's Home and Hill Affairs Department is to make the payments and the Commission to reimburse them, and that it is not known why the payments stopped. The 19 tribunals were set up by the Commission in March on the Supreme Court's orders, and the judges sit at the campus of the Syama Prasad Mookerjee National Institute of Water and Sanitation at Joka.
court-90.response: The report carries no statement from the state government, the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission, and does not say whether the tribunals sat on 19 November.
court-90.headline: Fresh hurdle for SIR tribunal: Staff go on strike after salary non-payment

court-91.case: Network of Women in Media, India v. Union of India and others, W.P.(C) No. 1361 of 2026, and connected petitions on the police's treatment of journalists covering the protests against the Chief Election Commissioner in October, Supreme Court (court-36, court-62, court-83)
court-91.claim: Newslaundry set the accounts of journalists detained during the protests against the Chief Election Commissioner in October against the Delhi Police's counter-affidavit in the Supreme Court (court-83), in a report of 20 November. The affidavit says some journalists were mistakenly identified as protesters in the absence of conspicuously displayed identification or accreditation, and that each was released as soon as their credentials were ascertained. Newslaundry reports journalists saying they were released only after a senior officer phoned or when a vehicle broke down. The affidavit says Ryan Thomas of The Caravan was not detained or kept at any holding facility on 11 October and was merely removed from the site, and that the medico-legal case is under investigation. Thomas told Newslaundry that he was holding up his press card when he was put in a detention bus, and that he was beaten in the bus and then in a jeep. He obtained a medico-legal certificate at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, which Newslaundry says does not record that the police caused the injury. He said he had filed no FIR and would send the police a legal notice. Ayush Tiwari of Scroll said he was detained at 11 am on 10 October while wearing his press card and could leave after about an hour and a half, when the bus he was in caught fire near Paharganj police station. Newslaundry says three of its reporters and an intern were detained on 10 October. One of them, Ashwine Singh, said he showed the police his card and that this happened between 11:30 am and noon. Newslaundry says its reporters were released after a senior officer called about their identity, and puts the whole incident at about three to four hours. Suhail Muhammad of 24 News said he and his cameraperson were driven around for about 30 minutes before the bus stopped in Connaught Place and they could leave. The affidavit calls false the petitioners' contention that the police arbitrarily seized media equipment. Rajwinder Singh and Lakhwinder Singh, who run the channel The Mike Report, said the police took their camera, that it took them at least three to four days to get it back, and that they were given no seizure memo. On the complaints of four women journalists, Newslaundry reports the police as saying the inquiry was concluded for lack of corroboration, and says one complainant has gone to court.
court-91.response: The affidavit is the police's reply to the petitions, and the journalists' accounts are their own. Newslaundry says it asked the Delhi Police's public relations officer and the Deputy Commissioner of Police, New Delhi, for a response and would update its report when one came.
court-91.headline: Anti-SIR protest: Journalists dispute Delhi Police’s affidavit to Supreme Court

court-92.case: West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals of retired judges (court-18, court-67, court-90)
court-92.claim: The retired Calcutta High Court judge Kanchan Chakraborty, appointed about two months ago to West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunal that hears appeals from Kolkata, resumed office in the past week and began hearing appeals, The Times of India reported on 22 November. The paper says he fell ill within days of his appointment and that the puja vacation followed. Around 1 lakh appeals from the area of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, which has 17 Assembly constituencies, are pending before that tribunal. The paper says the hearing and disposal of Kolkata's appeals had been erratic since the first judge appointed to it, the former Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court T.S. Sivagnanam, resigned in May. It reports that the retired judge Mir Dara Sheko, who heard appeals from West Burdwan, now hears those from South 24 Parganas in place of Ranjit Kumar Bag, who resigned, and that Narayan Chandra Seal, appointed to the tribunals later, hears the appeals from West Burdwan. The paper says no one has been appointed in place of Biswajit Basu, who heard appeals from part of Murshidabad and resigned this month (court-67).
court-92.response: The report carries no statement from the Commission, the Chief Electoral Officer or the tribunals, and does not say on what day the judge resumed or how many appeals he has heard. A voter from south Kolkata whose name was deleted and who has appealed told the paper that the appointment of a new judge was welcome and that he hoped the appeals would be cleared before the elections to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, which the paper says may have been pushed back.
court-92.headline: Deleted Kolkata voters pin hopes as SIR judge resumes regular hearing

court-93.case: Network of Women in Media, India v. Union of India and others, W.P.(C) No. 1361 of 2026, and connected petitions on the police's treatment of journalists covering the protests against the Chief Election Commissioner in October, Supreme Court (court-36, court-62, court-83, court-91)
court-93.claim: The Network of Women in Media, India filed a rejoinder in the Supreme Court on 21 November to the Delhi Police's counter-affidavit (court-83) in its petition on the police's treatment of journalists covering the protests against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, in October, Newslaundry, LiveLaw, The New Indian Express and Scroll reported. It says the affidavit itself reveals the extent of the interference complained of, and Newslaundry reports it as saying that paragraphs of the affidavit read like a catalogue of admissions and that terms such as mistaken identity, verification and released upon identification soften the description of actual restraint. LiveLaw reports it as arguing that the police's own account, that journalists were removed from protest sites, put in police vehicles for verification and released once identified, establishes the interference with their liberty and their work, and that their eventual release does not answer whether the restraint was lawful. On the police's reliance on section 172 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, the rejoinder says the power arises only where a person disobeys an earlier lawful direction, and that the affidavit does not identify, incident by incident, the direction given, the officer who gave it, what the journalist did to disobey it or why removal was needed in place of a less restrictive measure. LiveLaw reports it as citing section 65 of the Delhi Police Act and the Supreme Court's judgment in D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal on the safeguards of arrest and detention, and Newslaundry reports it as saying that section 29 of that Act only names the officers who can issue orders regulating assemblies and public places. The rejoinder calls the police's use of the term reel-makers a retrospective justification, says the question is what the person was doing, and says the freedom to gather news cannot be made conditional on accreditation, employment with a recognised media organisation or an employer's identity card. On the complaints of sexual harassment from the protest of 3 October, which the police say the Crime Branch closed, it says the closure reinforces the case for an inquiry independent of the police whose personnel are complained against, and that a complainant's reluctance to pursue a complaint is no conclusive proof that the conduct did not occur. LiveLaw reports that it also cites the National Human Rights Commission's notice of 8 October to the Delhi Police Commissioner on the reported harassment of three women journalists. The police had said that 3,747 women personnel were deployed by day and 664 at night and that women taken away in police vehicles were accompanied by a woman officer, and the rejoinder says these figures do not identify who handled the women journalists. It says the police could have set up press areas, liaison officers, safe routes and protective helmets at a protest planned in advance, asks the Court to reject the police's plea to dismiss the petitions, and seeks safeguards, independent scrutiny and the production of contemporaneous records.
court-93.response: The rejoinder is the petitioner's answer to the police's affidavit. None of the reports carries a reply from the Delhi Police or gives a date for the next hearing.
court-93.headline: ‘Catalogue of admissions’: Journalists’ body says Delhi Police affidavit admits the interference it denies

court-95.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal), on West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals, Supreme Court (court-18, court-38, court-47, court-67, court-92)
court-95.claim: The bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana directed West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals on 23 November 2026 to divide the appeals before them into two groups, the appeals of electors whose names were deleted and the appeals against the inclusion of names, and to give the first group preference in final disposal, LiveLaw, Hindustan Times and The Times of India reported. The order says the appeals against inclusion involve no urgency and may for the time being be deferred. The Court directed that among the appeals of deleted electors those from the constituencies of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation be given priority, because the municipal elections are due. LiveLaw and Hindustan Times report that it directed the Election Commission to increase the strength of the tribunals in consultation with the Calcutta High Court, which Hindustan Times gives as the High Court's Chief Justice. The Times of India reports the direction as one to the High Court's Chief Justice, in consultation with the Commission, to increase the number of tribunals from the present 19. The Court asked the Commission to find other premises for the tribunals at different places in Kolkata. Hindustan Times reports that of the 38.31 lakh appeals filed, 22.21 lakh are by electors seeking to have their names restored and 16.10 lakh challenge inclusions, and that the 16.10 lakh were filed by officials of the office of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer. Prashant Bhushan, for the petitioners, told the bench that only a little over one lakh appeals had been decided and that 93% of those decided had gone in favour of the deleted electors, Hindustan Times and LiveLaw reported. The Times of India reports him as saying that more than 90% of the 1.4 lakh appeals decided had been allowed. He said that more than two lakh electors from the Kolkata municipal area had been excluded and that their appeals were pending. The senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan argued that the Chief Electoral Officer had no authority in law to file the appeals against inclusion, because under Rule 23 an appeal from a registration officer's decision lies to an officer the Commission designates, and LiveLaw reports him calling it an appeal from the Election Commission to itself.
court-95.response: Hindustan Times reports that the Commission's affidavit of October in the Supreme Court said the appeals against inclusion were filed by officers of the Chief Electoral Officer's office in their statutory capacity under the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and that the matters had not been brought before the Commission, and that the affidavit did not identify anyone who authorised them. No report gives a submission by the Commission's counsel on the tribunals at this hearing, and none gives a next date.
court-95.headline: West Bengal SIR | Defer Appeals Against Inclusions, Prioritise Appeals Filed By Deleted Voters : Supreme Court To Appellate Tribunals

court-96.case: Application by Prasenjit Bose in W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal), on welfare benefits for deleted electors, Supreme Court (court-95)
court-96.claim: The bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana issued notice on 23 November 2026 on an application by Prasenjit Bose, who chairs the SIR panel of the West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee, in the West Bengal SIR matter, LiveLaw reported. The application asks the Court to direct the state to withdraw all notifications restricting the access of electors deleted in the revision to welfare benefits, and names the Annapurna Yojana, the Public Distribution System and OBC certificates. The Times of India reports that the Court asked the state government to respond to the allegation that electors deleted in the revision are being denied rations and benefits under welfare schemes. Gopal Sankaranarayanan and Prashant Bhushan, for the petitioners, said the state government was taking the entitlements away. Justice Bagchi said the Court had already clarified that exclusion from the roll should not affect other entitlements, called the complaint an independent cause of action and suggested that it be raised in a separate writ petition. Sankaranarayanan pointed to a state notification of 4 June providing that beneficiaries of the Public Distribution System be verified and deleted on the basis of the revision's outcome, and Bhushan said that the Chief Minister of West Bengal had said deleted electors would be deprived of the benefits. Justice Bagchi said that this was in the nature of a statement by a political person and that an individual who was actually deprived could approach the High Court, and the Chief Justice said that any person affected could approach the High Court. The petitioners asked for a one-line clarification from the Court in place of fresh litigation in the High Court.
court-96.response: The Solicitor General, Tushar Mehta, said that bald assertions unaccompanied by facts should not be made for political purposes, LiveLaw reported, and The Times of India reports him saying that the petitioners had not cited a single example. Justice Bagchi replied that there was no bald assertion because the petitioners were pointing to a government notification, and said the Court would see whether it was being given effect. D.S. Naidu, for the Commission, said the Court had already made such observations many times. No report gives a date for the state's reply.
court-96.headline: Petitioner Urges Supreme Court To Clarify SIR Deletion Won't Lead To Denial Of State Welfare Benefits

court-97.case: The State of West Bengal and another v. Dipu Das and others, the state government's appeal against the Calcutta High Court division bench's order on the Kolkata Municipal Corporation elections and the delimitation of its wards, Supreme Court (court-37, court-38, court-95)
court-97.claim: The bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana said on 25 November 2026 that it was inclined to stay an order of a Calcutta High Court division bench that restrained West Bengal's State Election Commission from issuing a notification for the Kolkata Municipal Corporation elections until a single judge decides a challenge to the delimitation of the corporation's wards, PTI reported. The delimitation may raise the number of wards from 144 to 209. The bench said the writ petition before the single judge would be directed to be transferred to the division bench, which would pass a fresh order, and it asked the Solicitor General, Tushar Mehta, to seek instructions by 30 November. LawTrend reports that the bench also indicated that the elections could remain on hold until the division bench forms a view, and that the Court has not yet stayed the High Court's order. The petitioner in the High Court, Dipu Das, a former councillor of the CPI(M), alleged that the delimitation exercise was undertaken on the basis of electoral rolls instead of the actual population, and so left a substantial number of residents out of consideration. He asked the High Court to declare the whole exercise of fixing the number of wards void and to quash the gazette notification of 11 September expanding the wards. He also said the corporation had no elected council and that its former chairperson had been appointed its administrator after the House was dissolved on 8 June. The single judge refused an interim stay on 29 October and Das appealed to the division bench. PTI reports the division bench's order as saying that the state government could allow its chosen administrator to make a tailor-made recommendation and then be bound by it, in effect allowing the government to recommend amendments to itself, and that section 601 of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation Act vests in the corporation the power to make a binding recommendation on the delimitation of its own wards. The order said its observations were tentative as far as the final disposal of the writ petition was concerned.
court-97.response: Neither PTI nor LawTrend gives a submission on the merits by the state government, the State Election Commission or the petitioner at this hearing. The Election Commission is not reported as a party.
