PTI gives 30 November as the date by which the Solicitor General is to seek instructions, and LawTrend says the Court will consider the matter further after that. Neither gives a time or an item number for a hearing.
court-97.headline: SC ‘inclined’ to stay Calcutta HC order deferring civic polls till decision on ward delimitation

court-98.case: The petitions alleging illegal detention of protesters during the protests against the Chief Election Commissioner in October, Supreme Court (court-36, court-83, protest-40)
court-98.claim: The Supreme Court directed the Centre and the Government of Delhi on 25 November 2026 to file a comprehensive response to the petitions alleging the illegal detention of protesters during the demonstrations of October seeking the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, Bar and Bench reported. Bar and Bench's post on X and United News of India's both give the time allowed as 10 days. Bar and Bench's standfirst says the Court passed the direction after it was told that responses to the petitions alleging illegal detention had yet to be filed. United News of India reports that the bench, headed by the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, was told by the Additional Solicitor General, Aishwarya Bhati, that affidavits had been filed in the habeas corpus petitions and that responses to the petitions on the detentions were still pending. It reports that the bench said any rejoinder could be filed within one week after that.
court-98.response: Neither the open part of Bar and Bench's report nor United News of India's post gives a submission by the Centre, the Government of Delhi or the Delhi Police beyond the Additional Solicitor General's account of the affidavits, and neither gives a date on which the petitions will next be heard.
court-98.headline: Supreme Court seeks Centre's response to petitions over detentions during October protest against CEC

court-99.case: West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals of retired judges (court-18, court-67, court-90, court-92, court-95)
court-99.claim: The judges of West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals have been given the option of working from home, The Telegraph reported on 25 November 2026, citing sources it does not name. Business Today reported the same day, following The Telegraph. A source in the tribunal told the paper that the judges had received calls from what the source called the state election commission, through the nodal officers for the tribunals, asking whether they would be comfortable working from home. The tribunals sit at SPM-Niwas, a central government institute at Joka on the southern edge of Kolkata, and the paper says several judges have complained of the long commute. It says at least a couple of judges are reported to have said they would work from home if the poll panel arranged suitable infrastructure and enough staff. An official said one judge who spends four hours travelling between his home and Joka welcomed the option but said it had to be backed by adequate staff and their transport to and from his home. A source attached to one of the 19 tribunals said its presiding judge could not hear more than 10 to 12 appeals a day because of logistical problems, and an official said the judge starts work around 11 am and that work ends by 4.30 pm because the staff have to leave. The paper says four buses carry the tribunals' staff between Joka and Howrah, Sealdah, Baruipur and Diamond Harbour (court-90). Officials in the tribunals said the judges would for now hear only the appeals against the removal of names. The Supreme Court directed on 23 November that those appeals be given preference (court-95).
court-99.response: The account of the option and of the tribunals' working day comes from sources and officials the papers do not name, and the report gives no statement from the Chief Electoral Officer, the State Election Commission or the Election Commission. It does not say whether any judge has begun to work from home or whether the arrangement has been approved.
court-99.headline: Work-from-home option for Bengal SIR tribunals: Efficiency cited on hearings

form7-102.claim: A two and a half month old infant in Cooch Behar district has been denied a birth certificate as a result of the deletion of her father's name from the roll during the revision, The Hindu reported on 24 November. The girl was born on 9 September at the sub-divisional hospital in Dinhata. The paper reports that when her parents approached the hospital and the panchayat office for the certificate, they were asked to arrange residential verification from the panchayat pradhan or the MLA, that the office of the MLA for Dinhata, Ajoy Roy, refused the father's request for the verification, and that the father was told the certificate could not be issued because his name had been deleted from the roll. The father told the paper that an official from the MLA's office said he was a Bangladeshi national and would first have to register through the National Register of Citizens. He said he has lived in India since his birth, that his house was built by his grandfather, and that he had shown all his documents and was still refused. He said the block development officer of Sahebganj refused a similar request on the same grounds. The paper reports that the names of three of his sisters were also deleted, that the Commission had called them for a hearing citing a logical discrepancy that six other persons had given the name of his father, and that his parents, his wife and an elder sister are on the roll. He has appealed to a tribunal to have his name included. The Association for Protection of Civil Rights said in a statement that birth registration is a statutory obligation, that every child has the right to immediate registration and legal identity under Article 7 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, and that a child's right to legal identity must not be linked to the electoral status of her parents, and demanded that the government provide the certificate at once. The Wire carried the same account on 25 November. On 23 November the Supreme Court issued notice on an application asking it to direct the state to withdraw notifications that restrict the welfare benefits of electors deleted in the revision (court-96).
form7-102.response: The report carries no statement from the MLA, his office, the panchayat, the block development officer, the hospital or the Chief Electoral Officer. The paper states the refusal by the MLA's office in its own words. The official's remark on nationality and the refusal by the block development officer are the father's account.
form7-102.headline: Deletion of father’s name from voter list poses hurdle to infant’s birth certificate

form7-48.case: W.P. No. 31887 of 2026 and W.P. No. 31893 of 2026, two BJP booth agents' petitions, Karnataka High Court
form7-48.claim: The Karnataka High Court stayed proceedings in two FIRs against two BJP booth agents accused over bulk Form 7s against voters in Bengaluru's Malleshwaram constituency, Bar and Bench reported. The judge said the FIRs looked premature because the registration officer had not yet decided the Form 7s. One FIR concerns applications against 778 voters in ward 64 and the other objections against 136 voters in ward 45.
form7-48.response: The State said the allegations of impersonation and forgery needed investigation and that the agents filed more applications than allowed. The complainant's counsel said the bulk filing was a conspiracy aimed at OBC and SC/ST voters.
form7-48.headline: SIR: Karnataka High Court grants relief to BJP booth agents booked for attempting to delete voters

form7-49.case: CRL.P 102783/2026 and connected matters, a BJP functionary's petition, Karnataka High Court at Dharwad
form7-49.claim: The Karnataka High Court at Dharwad told the police on 8 October to take no coercive steps until 13 October against a BJP functionary and two supporters booked over Form 7s against voters in Belagavi, LiveLaw and Bar and Bench reported. A Congress block agent's complaint, as the police record it, alleges they handed about 198 fabricated Form 7s to the booth officer. On 13 October Justice Venkatesh Naik T stayed the investigation until the next hearing, citing a coordinate bench's stay in similar cases on 9 October, Bar and Bench reported. The Court allowed the State to seek to have the order modified or vacated, and posted the matter for 29 October.
form7-49.response: The Government Pleader sought time to file objections and the latest investigation report.
form7-49.headline: Karnataka High Court Grants Interim Protection To BJP Leader Booked Over Alleged Attempt To Delete Muslim Voters' Names During SIR

form7-58.claim: The office of the North East Delhi District Election Officer, Ajay Kumar, said on 31 October that election officers would visit every elector against whom a Form 7 objection had been filed in the Mustafabad constituency to check the claim before any name is deleted, and that it would act under the rules against objectors whose claims were found false or mischievous, The Hindu reported. The office was replying to a post on X that shared the paper's report of 30 October, which found all 28 electors at polling booth 129 against whom a booth level agent appointed by the BJP had filed objections, citing absence, a permanent shift or death, living at their registered addresses. The paper reported 843 Form 7 applications in the constituency by 28 October, and 572 of them filed by 19 of the BJP's booth level agents, all against Muslim electors, in 24 parts of the constituency. With 118 more filed on 29 and 30 October the total reached 961, and 684 of them, 71%, were filed by the BJP's agents, the paper reported from the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's list of applications. Officials told the paper the agents' applications carried no undertaking from the agent and were not in the prescribed format. Nine more applications naming the agent at booth 129 as objector appeared on the list of 30 October.
form7-58.response: The District Election Officer's office said no bulk applications beyond the prescribed limits had been received in Mustafabad, online or on paper, and gave a figure of 832 Forms 7 and 8, 102 of them Form 8, filed in the constituency up to 30 October, which differs from the public list. Senior officials of the Commission told the paper that agents who file as objectors without the undertaking for bulk filing are held to the limit of ten applications set on 9 October. The agent named at booth 129 had told the paper he did not file the forms and was neither a booth level agent nor associated with any party. Neither report says how the paper established that the electors were Muslim. Ali Mehdi, the Congress candidate for Mustafabad in the 2025 Assembly election, said in a post on X that he had complained to the North East Delhi Deputy Commissioner of Police and sought an FIR against the BJP's agents.
form7-58.headline: After voters found at Delhi addresses, DEO orders field verification of deletion claims

form7-60.claim: Twenty people registered with the Election Commission as the BJP's booth level agents are named as objectors in 787 Form 7 applications in Delhi's Mustafabad constituency, at least 77% of the 1,021 deletion applications filed there so far, The Hindu reported on 4 November from the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's public list. The paper reports that all 787 are against Muslim electors and that they are 94% of the 837 deletion applications filed by third parties. It contacted all 20 agents, and 16 of them denied filing or signing any of the forms. One agent named in 32 applications told the paper he had complained to the party and resigned as its agent, and the paper reports that it checked with the area's booth level officer that the electors in those applications live at their registered addresses. One agent named in 57 applications said he had filed them and put his own total at 500 forms. Two agents could not be reached, and the number listed for another was a wrong number. The forms naming the 20 agents were filed without the undertaking or the format prescribed for an agent's bulk filing, the paper has learnt, and all of them were received after the Commission set a limit of ten Form 7 applications for each elector on 9 October. An agent named in 56 applications said the Electoral Registration Officer's office called him on 3 November about the objections and that he told it he had not filed them.
form7-60.response: The District Election Officer, the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission did not answer the paper's questions. The District Election Officer had said earlier that every deletion claim would be verified in person by the booth level officer and the registration officer or an assistant, and that action would be taken against claims found false or mischievous (form7-58). The Commission's directive of 9 October, as the paper quotes it, says a registration officer who finds a Form 7 complaint false or fabricated shall act against the applicant under the Representation of the People Act. The report does not say how the paper established that the electors were Muslim.
form7-60.headline: Who filed 77% of Form 7s in Delhi’s Mustafabad? BJP BLAs named as ‘objectors’ deny them

form7-61.outlet: Anjali Bhardwaj on X, posting the petitioners' letter of 5 November 2026 to the Chief Election Commissioner, the two Election Commissioners and Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer
form7-61.claim: Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, the petitioners in the Supreme Court case on Delhi's revision (W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, court-54), wrote on 5 November 2026 to the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, the Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, and Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer, Ashok Kumar, about The Hindu's report on Form 7 applications in Mustafabad (form7-60). Their letter gives the report's figures, that at least 787 of the 1,021 deletion applications filed there were in the names of 20 booth level agents appointed by the BJP, all against Muslim electors, and that 16 of the 20 denied filling, signing or knowing of the forms. The letter says this indicates that their identities appear to have been forged and used fraudulently without their consent. It asks the Commission and the Chief Electoral Officer to direct the registration of FIRs under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including for forgery, criminal impersonation, identity fraud and false declarations, and to audit every Form 7 submitted in every Delhi constituency during the revision to check whether the objectors named authorised and signed them. After investigation, it asks for action under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 against everyone who knowingly made a false or fabricated declaration in a Form 7. It asks for an immediate stay on every deletion arising from a third-party Form 7 until the electors concerned and the objectors named have been independently verified. It also asks for a public report of how many Form 7 applications were received, how many were confirmed on verification and how many were found to be fraudulent, and for every Form 7 received during the revision to be published on the Chief Electoral Officer's website so that people can check whether one was filed in their name.
form7-61.response: No reply from the Commission or the Chief Electoral Officer had been reported by 5 November. The Commission's directive of 9 October, as The Hindu quotes it, says a registration officer who finds a Form 7 complaint false or fabricated shall act against the applicant under the Representation of the People Act (form7-60). The North East Delhi District Election Officer had said on 31 October that every Form 7 in Mustafabad would be verified in the field before any name is deleted (form7-58).
form7-61.headline: The petitioners in the Delhi case ask the Commission for FIRs, an audit of every Form 7 and a stay on deletions from third-party Form 7s, after The Hindu's report on Mustafabad

form7-62.claim: The Electoral Registration Officer of Delhi's Mustafabad constituency lodged a police complaint on Friday 6 November seeking an FIR under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, against a booth level agent named as objector on 37 Form 7 applications, The Hindu reported. The North East Delhi District Election Officer, Ajay Kumar, told the paper that officials had verified its report of 30 October on polling part 129 (form7-58) and found 36 of the 37 forms false or fabricated. A press release from his office said that the booth level officer and the assistant registration officer had checked all 37, that three electors the forms gave as dead were found alive, and that the others were found living at their addresses. It said that verification of the other Form 7 applications was continuing. The paper's earlier report had found the agent registered with the BJP by the Commission's records. A senior police officer told Daijiworld that the complaint had been received and that an investigation was under way. The Delhi Congress leader Ali Mehdi told Daijiworld that he had complained on 31 October, naming 14 booth level agents, and handed a copy to the Chief Electoral Officer, and that the matter was formally registered only a week later.
form7-62.response: The Delhi BJP spokesperson, Praveen Shankar Kapoor, told Daijiworld that the party had not submitted any such forms, and that the booth level officer is responsible for checking every Form 7 before a name is deleted. The agent had told The Hindu earlier that he did not file the forms and was neither a booth level agent nor associated with any party (form7-58). The reports give no FIR number and do not say whether an FIR has been registered.
form7-62.headline: Delhi’s Mustafabad election official lodges police complaint seeking FIR over false Form 7s filing

form7-67.claim: The 796 Form 7 applications that name 20 booth level agents appointed by the BJP as objectors in Delhi's Mustafabad constituency are mostly concentrated in 25 of its 294 polling booths, in the neighbourhoods of Nehru Vihar, Dayalpur and Chandu Nagar, The Hindu reported on 10 November. The paper reports that all of them are against Muslim electors and that they are over 76% of the 1,044 deletion applications received in the constituency up to 4 November, from the published data. The applications give absence, a permanent shift or death as the reason, and the paper found at least 87 of the electors named living at their registered addresses. The paper reports, from an analysis of records and interviews with local BJP workers, that the 25 booths appeared to have been selected because they had a sizeable Muslim population and, by the workers' claims, few names left off the draft roll. BJP leaders who spoke to it on condition of anonymity said that after the draft of 31 August party workers compared the number of names placed on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors in booths with a majority of Muslim electors and in booths with a majority of Hindu electors, prepared lists of Muslim electors, which the paper says it saw, and then concentrated on the 25 booths, where the agents began filing from the first week of October. The paper says it found copies of these booths' rolls, with the names of Muslim electors marked on them, with BJP workers in the area. It reports that the Commission's booth-wise figures do not bear out the workers' claim. By its count, names left off the draft averaged 274 a booth in Mustafabad and reached 538 at the most, and in most of the 25 booths they were close to the average. Parts 108 and 129, which it counts among the five booths with the fewest names left off the draft, carry 35 and 37 of the agents' applications. No application names a BJP agent in the other three, which BJP workers said were mostly Hindu. Nehru Vihar has the most applications, 496. The paper reports that none of the Form 7s received in Mustafabad came with the undertaking an agent must give.
form7-67.response: The Delhi BJP spokesperson, Praveen Shankar Kapoor, told the paper that the party's agents had not filed any Form 7s in Mustafabad, that the party had not directed any forms to be filed, and that booth level officers and the Commission would act on any objections under the rules. The BJP councillor for Nehru Vihar, Arun Bhati, said he was not authorised to speak about the applications, and said that some booths in Mustafabad had 300 to 500 votes deleted, which he said were coincidentally of Hindu voters, while others had fewer than 100, and that the two could not both be correct. The paper reports that officials maintain religious identity has no role in verification. The agent named in 57 applications told the paper he had filed them himself because the electors had shifted, and the councillor's brother, an agent named in 37, denied filing his. The report does not say how the paper established the religion of the electors or of each booth's population.
form7-67.headline: Delhi SIR: Why BJP BLAs’ voter deletion applications in Mustafabad focused on three neighbourhoods

form7-75.case: Three petitions by BJP booth level agents against FIRs over Form 7 applications, Crl.P. No. 15507 of 2026 (Mysuru), W.P. No. 32308 of 2026 (Jayanagar) and W.P. No. 32215 of 2026 (Kodagu), with the State's applications to vacate the stays in the two Malleshwaram petitions of 9 October, W.P. No. 31887 of 2026 and W.P. No. 31893 of 2026, Karnataka High Court (form7-48)
form7-75.claim: Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde of the Karnataka High Court on 17 November 2026 stayed further investigation in three more FIRs against BJP booth level agents over bulk Form 7 applications, Bar and Bench, LiveLaw and Hindustan Times reported. LiveLaw gives the three FIRs as one at the Narasimharaja police station in Mysuru against three agents, one at the Jayanagar police station in Bengaluru against two and one at the Shanivarasante police station in Kodagu against five, ten petitioners in all. With them the Court has stayed the investigation in five cases. In the two Malleshwaram cases (form7-48) the orders defer the State's applications to vacate the stays of 9 October and stay further investigation until further orders. Each order says that the inquiry by the registration officer under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 has to run its course first, and that the officer's finding may give the material to decide whether an FIR should be quashed or investigated. In the Malleshwaram and Jayanagar orders the Court said that the agents had not disowned their signatures on the forms and that the allegation of forgery could not be accepted at that stage. In those three cases and in Kodagu the Court directed the Election Commission, a respondent in each, to place on record the materials on its decisions on the Form 7 applications the agents filed. In the Mysuru case it directed the petitioners to add the State Election Commission as a respondent and directed that respondent to place the same materials on record. The complaints, as Bar and Bench and Hindustan Times report them, allege that the applications carried false information, forged signatures or impersonation, and some of them allege that the applications were aimed at Muslim electors. Bar and Bench gives the complaints' counts as 778 applications across eight polling stations in Malleshwaram, 5,698 applications in Jayanagar, 4,327 of them in Gurrappanapalya ward, 136 electors in Yeshwanthpur and 64 in Kodagu.
form7-75.response: The Advocate General, K Shashi Kiran Shetty, opposed the petitions for the State and argued that fake or forged applications could not be permitted during the revision, because the right to vote is a valuable right. The petitioners argued that booth level agents were entitled to file Form 7 objections for political parties and that the registration officer had to examine whether the objections were correct. The Court allowed the complainants to seek modification or vacation of the interim orders, and the State to seek modification once it receives the Commission's records, Bar and Bench reported. No next date was reported.
form7-75.headline: Karnataka High Court stays probe against 10 more persons accused of attempting to delete Muslim voters through Form 7

form7-99.case: Writ petition by four petitioners to quash the Suddaguntepalya police FIR of 7 October over Form 7 applications, W.P. No. 32768 of 2026, Karnataka High Court (form7-42, form7-75)
form7-99.claim: Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde of the Karnataka High Court declined on 20 November 2026 to stay the police investigation into an FIR over Form 7 applications filed to delete six electors from the roll in Bengaluru, and directed that the petitioners not be arrested and that no chargesheet be filed without the Court's leave, LawChakra and Bar and Bench reported. The Suddaguntepalya police registered the FIR on 7 October against the Jayanagar MLA of the BJP, C K Ramamurthy, and three others, under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and sections 217(b), 3(5), 336(2), 340(2) and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. The complainant alleges that Form 7 applications were filed to delete his name and those of five members of his family, who have lived at Old Gurappanapalya in Bengaluru for about 50 years, and that the MLA acknowledged in a conference call that an application had been submitted and said it would be withdrawn and corrected. LawChakra says these are allegations in the complaint and have not been tested. The petition, filed by four petitioners to quash the FIR, argued that they were already accused in the FIR the Jayanagar police registered on 5 October on a complaint by the former MLA Sowmya Reddy (form7-42), that a second FIR over the same exercise was not maintainable, and that the ingredients of forgery and of using forged documents were not made out. The Court issued notice to the complainant, asked the petitioners to serve the petition on the Election Commission's standing counsel and listed the case on 8 January 2027. On 17 November the same judge had stayed the investigation in three other FIRs over Form 7 applications (form7-75).
form7-99.response: The Additional State Public Prosecutor, Anoop Kumar, said the complaint required investigation, and that in earlier cases raising almost the same questions the State had said it would not arrest the petitioners, which would apply here as long as they cooperated with the probe, LawChakra reported. No report carries a statement by the MLA.
form7-99.headline: Karnataka High Court Refuses To Stay Form 7 Voter Deletion Probe, Bars Arrest Of Petitioners

protest-40.claim: The South First reported on the morning of 10 October that police sealed central Delhi before the Cockroach Janta Party's protest at Jantar Mantar demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation over the SIR. It said more than 1,000 people had been detained overnight and 45 Metro stations were shut, and that police detained CPI(M) leaders including Pinarayi Vijayan and John Brittas when they tried to march from Kerala House.
protest-40.response: No statement from the Commission was reported. Police told the protesters that a gathering of more than four people was not allowed.
protest-40.headline: Cockroach Janta Party protest: New Delhi sealed even before the first slogan

protest-46.case: Uday Bhanu Chib v. Union of India and Ors, Delhi High Court
protest-46.claim: The Delhi Police told the Delhi High Court on 13 October that it de-notified Jantar Mantar as the designated protest site, and identified three other sites, on the basis of the Supreme Court's order of 9 October, Bar and Bench reported. That order had said suitable sites where basic amenities could be provided to protesters should be identified, and left the decision to the competent authority. The submission came on Indian Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib's petition against the refusal of permission to protest at Jantar Mantar against the Chief Election Commissioner. Justice Amit Mahajan issued notice on three of its prayers, which challenge the police's reliance on its 2022 standing order and the 10-day advance notice for protests.
protest-46.response: The police said the petition had become infructuous because Jantar Mantar had been de-notified. On 15 October the Solicitor General told the Supreme Court that the decision followed the recommendations of a committee set up by the Union Home Ministry well before the Court's oral observations, Bar and Bench reported.
protest-46.headline: Decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as protest site taken after Supreme Court order: Delhi police to High Court

protest-47.case: Petition by the Delhi Kirana Committee and the Delhi Iron and Hardware Merchant Association, Supreme Court
protest-47.claim: Counsel for two traders' associations raised in the Supreme Court on 16 October their petition against the Cockroach Janta Party's call to unfurl the tricolour in Connaught Place's Central Park that evening, saying it would obstruct trade worth Rs 200 crore a day, The Wire reported. The party had called the protest after two of its leaders were arrested for waving the flag at Jantar Mantar. The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said it would act on compensation if the NDMC's restrictions were found disproportionate, noted that the Delhi High Court was hearing a similar matter, and listed the petition for 26 and 27 October, after the Dussehra break.
protest-47.response: The Wire says the petitions appear to be concerned with the protest itself, though counsel told the Court the NDMC had shut the place by a notice the night before, as LiveLaw reported. It carries the party founder's post on X that businesses suffer when the government shuts down a city and restricts its citizens' movement.
protest-47.headline: 'If NDMC Order Disproportionate, We'll Act': Supreme Court Lists Petition Against CJP Protest After Vacation

protest-48.case: A teacher's petition against his suspension from booth level officer duty, Punjab and Haryana High Court
protest-48.claim: The Punjab and Haryana High Court quashed the suspension of a teacher in Hisar district who had asked to be relieved of booth level officer duty after his wife died, and imposed costs of Rs 50,000 on the District Elementary Education Officer, Hisar and the Electoral Registration Officer for the Barwala constituency, Bar and Bench reported. Justice Harpreet Singh Brar found that the authorities appointed three substitutes for his booth without making sure any of them joined, and then suspended him for a duty he no longer held. The Court directed the Chief Electoral Officer, Haryana to make sure that a booth level officer who is replaced is told in writing whether he stands relieved.
protest-48.response: The authorities said he had never been relieved of the duty and had missed the SIR training. The Court found they could not state the date of the training, and noted that none of the three substitutes attended it either.
protest-48.headline: Punjab & Haryana High Court grants relief to teacher suspended for not joining SIR duty after wife's death

protest-51.case: Petition against a Leave India Notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office, Bombay High Court
protest-51.claim: A division bench of the Bombay High Court, Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna, on 2 November kept in abeyance until 7 December the Leave India Notice that the Foreigners Regional Registration Office issued on 14 October to an actor who is a United States citizen holding an Overseas Citizen of India card, The Hindu and The Indian Express reported. Police had detained him near August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai on 10 October at a protest demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner over the SIR. The actor filed an unconditional apology and an undertaking that he would not take part in any protest or influence others to take part. The bench said Overseas Citizen of India cardholders could not claim the same rights as citizens, and The Indian Express reports that it said he was not remotely affected by the SIR. It allowed him to stay in India until the registration office decides the notice after hearing his response, and listed the matter for 7 December.
protest-51.response: Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh, for the Union, argued that the actor had been involved in the protest from the start and had no legally enforceable right to remain in India. Senior advocate Venkatesh Dhond, for the actor, said he had gone to the site out of curiosity, had no link with the organisers and had not been heard before the notice was issued.
protest-51.headline: Bombay HC extends stay on [the actor's] ‘Leave India Notice’, seeks unconditional apology over SIR protest

protest-65.case: The petition of Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri on the Delhi SIR, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, Supreme Court (court-54, court-60)
protest-65.claim: Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, the petitioners in the Supreme Court case on Delhi's revision, wrote on 10 November 2026 to the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, and the Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, asking that the remedies in the Commission's letter of 6 November to seven states be given to every elector in the country who was left off a draft roll and placed on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors, The Wire reported. The letter of 6 November lets such electors in Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland seek inclusion on an enumeration form in place of Form 6. The petitioners write that these "vital remedies" must be extended to all voters in a similar legal standing. Citing 13.30 crore electors on the rolls before the revision who were left off the drafts across the country, they say the new safeguards help only the 4.52 crore in the seven states. They say the new procedure treats unequally the electors who filed Form 6 under the Commission's earlier instructions and were issued new EPIC numbers, because Form 6 carries a declaration that the applicant is a first-time voter, which the Supreme Court called a "structural incongruity" in the hearings on Delhi's revision (court-54). They ask that every elector on these lists be allowed to file an enumeration form, that the Form 6 applications such electors have already filed be cancelled and their original EPIC numbers restored, and that the Commission publish regular updates on a dashboard or in daily bulletins of how many electors on the lists have filed enumeration forms and how many have been approved.
protest-65.response: No reply from the Commission was reported by 11 November. The Commission's letter of 6 November says an elector in the seven states who has already filed Form 6 during the revision need not submit the enumeration form, and that the application is to be decided under its letter of 3 November (court-60), which says such a Form 6 is not false merely because the elector was enrolled before.
protest-65.headline: ECI Urged to Restore Old Voter IDs for All Excluded During SIR, Not Just In 7 States

protest-66.claim: Karnataka's State Election Commission directed the commissioners of the five city corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority to speed up the preparation of ward-wise electoral rolls for the elections to the five corporations, Deccan Herald reported on 12 November. In a communication dated 5 November, the State Election Commission told officials to base the rolls on the final Assembly rolls published on 27 October after the revision. Officials are to map electors' details to the notified ward boundaries and prepare the rolls in Excel format, with no more than 1,200 electors in a polling part, and are to send the ward rolls and related details to the State Election Commission by 12 November. The State Election Commission said the work was begun in accordance with the Supreme Court's directions, which set the end of December as the deadline for completing the elections.
protest-66.response: The direction is the State Election Commission's own. The report does not name the Supreme Court case or date its order, and it carries no statement from the state government or from the parties that asked for the local body elections to be held on the rolls from before the revision.
protest-66.headline: Karnataka: State Election Commission asks Bengaluru corporations to prepare ward-wise poll rolls

soft-53.claim: The Election Commission has taken the SIR declaration out of the online Form 6 on its ECINet portal in the states where the revision is still running, and the declaration is now on the portal as a separate form, The Indian Express reported on 4 November. The declaration sat between Sections J and K of the online form and asked an applicant to say whether their own name, or a parent's or grandparent's, was on the roll of the last intensive revision, and an applicant could not go on without answering it. The paper reports that the Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October (court-52) records a decision of its ER Division of 21 October that the online application would be in two parts, Form 6 and the SIR declaration, as the paper forms are, and that this is what the portal now shows. After the Commission's note of 26 September the declaration had been taken off the online form only in the states where the revision had ended. The paper also reports that four changes to ECINet that Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer, S. Chockalingam, sought in a letter of 24 September have been made. Personal hearings for electors sent notices over mapping or logical discrepancies are now held only in exceptional cases, with booth level officers collecting documents at home. Electors may give documents outside the listed categories. Registration officers can decide logical-discrepancy cases themselves without sending them to the District Election Officer. The upload of an extract from the previous SIR roll is no longer mandatory. The paper reports that applicants filing Form 6 in the special summary revision ordered for 17 states and union territories will not have to fill the SIR declaration. The paper reports that a committee to check whether ECINet complies with the applicable Acts and Rules was constituted by a circular of 14 October. It is headed by a Senior Deputy Election Commissioner and includes a second Senior Deputy Election Commissioner, a Deputy Election Commissioner, a director, four Chief Electoral Officers and two independent experts, from IIT Bombay and IISc Bengaluru. On Goa, the paper reports that the Chief Electoral Officer has been directed to see that the 97 electors left off the final roll are included. It reports that the affidavit says 88 of them have filled in Form 6 and had their applications accepted, that six are out of the country and that three hold Portuguese passports. On West Bengal, the paper reports that the affidavit does not give the number of appeals filed against the inclusion of electors, that the appeals have not been withdrawn, and that the affidavit says the electors concerned are on the rolls and voted in the recent Assembly elections.
soft-53.response: The Commission's counter affidavit, as the paper quotes it, maintains that Form 6 was never amended: "There is no substance in the contention that Form 6 has been amended by the Commission vide the SIR Orders." It says the declaration was placed inside the online Form 6 so that an applicant would need a single OTP and a single e-signature.
soft-53.headline: Election Commission completes Form 6 U-turn, drops SIR para a Commissioner called ‘illegal’

soft-65.claim: The Election Commission has changed its portal for West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals as the judges demanded, and the tribunals have begun uploading their orders again after a gap of nearly 45 days, sources told The Times of India, which reported it on 21 November. The dispute over the portal is recorded in soft-41 and soft-50. A source told the paper that orders have been uploaded again since 6 November. The paper reports that the changes let the judges decide which documents they consider in an appeal, and that the portal had let them consider or record only the 13 documents the Commission specified. A source in the tribunals said the use of the judges' Aadhaar numbers to upload orders has been replaced by their digital signatures, and the paper reports that the judges can now review their orders and add observations. The paper reports that the judges stopped logging in to the new portal on 21 September, and that their letter to the Commission in September said the tribunals had been practically rendered functionless and that the limit of 13 documents interfered with the functioning of quasi-judicial authorities. It says that the Supreme Court, when it ordered the tribunals set up in March, noted the 13 documents and said the list was indicative. On the strike by the tribunals' housekeeping staff of 19 November (court-90), a senior official in the Chief Electoral Officer's office told the paper on Friday, 20 November, that the 'matter has been solved', and a source in the tribunals said the strike did not continue that day.
soft-65.response: The account of the changes is from sources in the tribunals. The report carries no statement from the Commission and does not say on what date the portal was changed or how many orders have been uploaded since 6 November.
soft-65.headline: SIR tribunals resume order uploads after EC removes 13-document cap

up-01.case: Petition by Arvind Kumar Singh (Samajwadi Party) against the Election Commission of India, filed 28 November 2025, Supreme Court
up-01.claim: A Samajwadi Party member and former MP petitioned the Supreme Court on 28 November 2025 against the Commission's notification and the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer's orders under it, ThePrint reported. The petition said the timeline was unreasonable, set unreasonable work expectations and came without practical training, and asked for a searchable database.
up-01.headline: Fresh challenges to electoral roll revision in Assam & UP; SC notice to EC on Assam plea

up-26.case: The petitioners' interim application on Form 7 in the SIR matters concerning Uttar Pradesh, Kerala and Chhattisgarh, Supreme Court
up-26.claim: The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana directed on 30 October that the petitioners give the Election Commission's senior counsel a note of the irregularities in Form 7 applications in Uttar Pradesh that they say remain unresolved, and that the Commission then examine the facts, take corrective steps and file a compliance report, Bar and Bench reported. Counsel for the petitioners said the Court had asked the Commission on 5 August to respond to their interim application on Form 7 applications submitted before booth level officers in Chhattisgarh, Kerala and Uttar Pradesh, and that the issues in the first two states had since been addressed. He said 32 forms had been filed in one constituency against members of one community, that two forms on record were signed by the booth level officer, and that the Commission's affidavit carried material inconsistencies. He said FIRs had been directed in Telangana and Karnataka over similar filings and that nothing was done in Uttar Pradesh. Senior Advocate D.S. Naidu, for the Commission, said bulk Form 7 applications had been submitted and that officers checked them, found them false and did not act on them.
up-26.response: Naidu said the Commission can examine further claims once a formal complaint is filed. LawChakra notes that the Court made no finding on the petitioners' allegations.
up-26.headline: UP SIR: Supreme Court asks ECI to take steps against filing Form 7 applications in bulk for voter deletion

up-41.case: The Congress's application for the registration of an FIR against the District Election Officer of Pilibhit, filed 16 November 2026, in a court in Pilibhit
up-41.claim: The Congress filed an application in a court in Pilibhit on Monday, 16 November, seeking the registration of an FIR against the District Election Officer and a court-monitored investigation, Hindustan Times reported. The report gives the application as filed under Section 156(3) CrPC/BNSS, seeking directions to the police to register a case and investigate the role of the senior officials responsible for maintaining the roll. The party said the investigation so far had stopped at lower-level officials, two Sub-Divisional Magistrates and a computer operator, and that the District Election Officer, who is also the District Magistrate, had been the custodian of the roll. Its former state general secretary, Kumud Gangwar, said the manipulation could not have happened without the knowledge or negligence of the top officer. The party repeated its allegations that the names of 13,150 voters in Pilibhit Sadar were changed between July and September while their EPIC and serial numbers stayed the same, that about 884 voters still living in the constituency were deleted although they had submitted documents and that about 2,600 people who do not live at the given addresses were added. In total it alleges irregularities in 16,554 voter records in the seat. It says a team of 55 members checked the records of about 3.48 lakh voters booth by booth and found that a search for an EPIC number online brought up another person's details. It also alleges that many entries were made late at night, on Sundays and on public holidays, without a physical Form 8, supporting documents or a hearing by the Electoral Registration Officer. The report says the court was expected to hear the application on Wednesday, 18 November, and to seek a report from the police and the election authorities.
up-41.response: The report carries no reply from the District Election Officer, the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission. Whether the court heard the application on 18 November was not known at the time of reading.
up-41.headline: Voter roll ‘anomalies’: Congress moves Pilibhit court, seeks FIR against DEO

up-44.case: Kumud Gangwar's application against the then District Election Officer of Pilibhit and six others, registered as a miscellaneous case on 18 November 2026 by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Pilibhit
up-44.claim: The Chief Judicial Magistrate of Pilibhit, Mangal Dev Singh, ordered on Wednesday, 18 November, that the application of Kumud Gangwar be registered as a miscellaneous case, and called for inquiry reports before passing any order on it, Hindustan Times reported. Hindustan Times reported on 16 November that the Congress had applied to a court in Pilibhit for an FIR against the District Election Officer over the roll of Pilibhit Sadar, and quoted Gangwar, a former state general secretary of the party, on it (up-41). This report does not name the Congress or say whether the application before the magistrate is the one the party filed. The report says the application was made under Section 173(4) of the BNSS against the then District Election Officer of Pilibhit, Gyanendra Singh, and six other opposite parties, and that the complainant appeared before the court with counsel. The court said it would be proper to call for an inquiry report from the competent higher authorities before passing any order, and issued notices to the opposite parties to present their versions. For the former District Election Officer it sought a report from the divisional commissioner, Bareilly and Varanasi, as the report writes it. For the other opposite parties who are public servants it directed the District Magistrate of Pilibhit to hold a preliminary inquiry into the facts set out in the application and to send the report to the court by the next date, 2 December 2026. It directed the station house officer concerned to report by the same date whether any case had been registered at the police station on the matter. The report recalls the allegation that the names of 13,150 voters in Pilibhit Sadar were changed between July and September, after the roll of 10 April, while their EPIC numbers and serial numbers stayed the same.
up-44.response: The court has not ruled on the application, and the matter is next before it on 2 December 2026. The report carries no reply from the former District Election Officer, the other opposite parties, the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission.
up-44.headline: SIR row: Pilibhit court seeks inquiry reports on plaint against ex-DEO, others

list-01.matter: A petition against deletions in Maharashtra's revision, W.P.(C) No. 1330 of 2026. The Court issued notice to the Election Commission on 26 October.
list-01.due: The petition is listed for hearing. On 26 October the Court declined to extend the time for claims and objections or to stop the final roll before hearing the Commission.
list-01.quote: A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana heard Writ Petition (Civil) No. 1330 of 2026 on October 26, 2026, and listed it for November 5, 2026.

hi.matter: महाराष्ट्र के पुनरीक्षण में नाम हटाए जाने के ख़िलाफ़ याचिका, W.P.(C) No. 1330 of 2026। अदालत ने 26 अक्टूबर को निर्वाचन आयोग को नोटिस जारी किया।
hi.due: याचिका सुनवाई के लिए सूचीबद्ध है। 26 अक्टूबर को अदालत ने आयोग को सुने बिना दावों और आपत्तियों का समय बढ़ाने या अंतिम सूची रोकने से इनकार किया।

ur.matter: مہاراشٹر کی نظرثانی میں نام حذف کیے جانے کے خلاف درخواست، W.P.(C) No. 1330 of 2026۔ عدالت نے 26 اکتوبر کو الیکشن کمیشن کو نوٹس جاری کیا۔
ur.due: درخواست سماعت کے لیے فہرست میں ہے۔ 26 اکتوبر کو عدالت نے کمیشن کو سنے بغیر دعووں اور اعتراضات کی مدت بڑھانے یا حتمی فہرست روکنے سے انکار کیا۔

te.matter: మహారాష్ట్ర సవరణలో పేర్ల తొలగింపుపై పిటిషన్, W.P.(C) No. 1330 of 2026. కోర్టు అక్టోబర్ 26న ఎన్నికల సంఘానికి నోటీసు జారీ చేసింది.
te.due: పిటిషన్ విచారణకు జాబితాలో ఉంది. అక్టోబర్ 26న కోర్టు సంఘం వాదన వినకుండా క్లెయిములు, అభ్యంతరాల గడువు పొడిగించడానికి గానీ తుది జాబితాను ఆపడానికి గానీ నిరాకరించింది.

ta.matter: மகாராஷ்டிர திருத்தத்தில் பெயர்கள் நீக்கப்பட்டதை எதிர்த்த மனு, W.P.(C) No. 1330 of 2026. நீதிமன்றம் அக்டோபர் 26 அன்று தேர்தல் ஆணையத்துக்கு நோட்டீஸ் அனுப்பியது.
ta.due: மனு விசாரணைக்குப் பட்டியலிடப்பட்டுள்ளது. அக்டோபர் 26 அன்று ஆணையத்தின் தரப்பைக் கேட்காமல் கோரிக்கைகள் மற்றும் ஆட்சேபனைகளுக்கான காலத்தை நீட்டிக்கவோ இறுதிப் பட்டியலை நிறுத்தவோ நீதிமன்றம் மறுத்தது.

bn.matter: মহারাষ্ট্রের সংশোধনে নাম বাদ দেওয়ার বিরুদ্ধে আবেদন, W.P.(C) No. 1330 of 2026। আদালত 26 অক্টোবর নির্বাচন কমিশনকে নোটিস দেয়।
bn.due: আবেদনটি শুনানির তালিকায় আছে। 26 অক্টোবর আদালত কমিশনের বক্তব্য না শুনে দাবি ও আপত্তির সময় বাড়াতে বা চূড়ান্ত তালিকা আটকাতে অস্বীকার করে।

list-03.matter: The petitions alleging that decisions of the Election Commission, those on the revision among them, were taken without the agreement of the two Election Commissioners, led by W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026.
list-03.due: The lead petition is listed for admission as item 26 in the Chief Justice's court, before the Chief Justice, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana. The court sits from 10:30 am. Seven connected petitions are listed with it, among them the petitions of Asaduddin Owaisi, of Rahul Gandhi and others, of Digvijaya Singh and of Dola Sen.

hi.matter: वे याचिकाएँ जिनमें आरोप है कि निर्वाचन आयोग के फ़ैसले, पुनरीक्षण से जुड़े फ़ैसलों समेत, दोनों निर्वाचन आयुक्तों की सहमति के बिना लिए गए। मुख्य याचिका W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026 है।
hi.due: मुख्य याचिका मुख्य न्यायाधीश की अदालत में आइटम 26 के रूप में दाखिले (एडमिशन) के लिए सूचीबद्ध है, मुख्य न्यायाधीश, जस्टिस जॉयमाल्य बागची और जस्टिस वी. मोहना की पीठ के सामने। अदालत सुबह 10:30 बजे से बैठती है। उसके साथ सात जुड़ी हुई याचिकाएँ सूचीबद्ध हैं, जिनमें असदुद्दीन ओवैसी, राहुल गांधी और अन्य, दिग्विजय सिंह और डोला सेन की याचिकाएँ शामिल हैं।

ur.matter: وہ درخواستیں جن میں الزام ہے کہ الیکشن کمیشن کے فیصلے، نظرثانی سے متعلق فیصلوں سمیت، دونوں الیکشن کمشنروں کی رضامندی کے بغیر کیے گئے۔ مرکزی درخواست W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026 ہے۔
ur.due: مرکزی درخواست چیف جسٹس کی عدالت میں آئٹم 26 کے طور پر داخلے کے لیے فہرست میں ہے، چیف جسٹس، جسٹس جوئے مالیہ باگچی اور جسٹس وی موہنا کی بنچ کے سامنے۔ عدالت صبح 10:30 بجے سے بیٹھتی ہے۔ اس کے ساتھ سات منسلک درخواستیں فہرست میں ہیں، جن میں اسد الدین اویسی، راہل گاندھی اور دیگر، دگ وجے سنگھ اور ڈولا سین کی درخواستیں شامل ہیں۔

te.matter: సవరణకు సంబంధించిన నిర్ణయాలతో సహా ఎన్నికల సంఘం నిర్ణయాలు ఇద్దరు ఎన్నికల కమిషనర్ల అంగీకారం లేకుండా తీసుకున్నారని ఆరోపించే పిటిషన్లు. ప్రధాన పిటిషన్ W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026.
te.due: ప్రధాన పిటిషన్ ప్రధాన న్యాయమూర్తి కోర్టులో అంశం 26గా, ప్రధాన న్యాయమూర్తి, జస్టిస్ జోయ్‌మాల్య బాగ్చీ, జస్టిస్ వి. మోహన ధర్మాసనం ముందు అడ్మిషన్ కోసం జాబితాలో ఉంది. కోర్టు ఉదయం 10:30కి ప్రారంభమవుతుంది. దానితో పాటు ఏడు అనుబంధ పిటిషన్లు జాబితాలో ఉన్నాయి. వాటిలో అసదుద్దీన్ ఒవైసీ, రాహుల్ గాంధీ తదితరులు, దిగ్విజయ సింగ్, డోలా సేన్ పిటిషన్లు ఉన్నాయి.

ta.matter: திருத்தம் தொடர்பான முடிவுகள் உட்பட தேர்தல் ஆணையத்தின் முடிவுகள் இரண்டு தேர்தல் ஆணையர்களின் ஒப்புதல் இல்லாமல் எடுக்கப்பட்டதாகக் கூறும் மனுக்கள். முதன்மை மனு W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026.
ta.due: முதன்மை மனு தலைமை நீதிபதியின் நீதிமன்றத்தில் வரிசை எண் 26 ஆக, தலைமை நீதிபதி, நீதிபதி ஜாய்மால்யா பாக்சி, நீதிபதி வி. மோகனா அமர்வு முன் அனுமதிக்காகப் பட்டியலிடப்பட்டுள்ளது. நீதிமன்றம் காலை 10:30 மணிக்குத் தொடங்குகிறது. அதனுடன் ஏழு இணைந்த மனுக்கள் பட்டியலிடப்பட்டுள்ளன. அவற்றில் அசதுத்தீன் ஒவைசி, ராகுல் காந்தி மற்றும் பிறர், திக்விஜய் சிங், டோலா சென் ஆகியோரின் மனுக்களும் அடங்கும்.

bn.matter: যে আবেদনগুলিতে অভিযোগ, সংশোধন সংক্রান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত সহ নির্বাচন কমিশনের সিদ্ধান্ত দুই নির্বাচন কমিশনারের সম্মতি ছাড়াই নেওয়া হয়েছে। মূল আবেদন W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026।
bn.due: মূল আবেদনটি প্রধান বিচারপতির আদালতে 26 নম্বর আইটেম হিসেবে প্রধান বিচারপতি, বিচারপতি জয়মাল্য বাগচী ও বিচারপতি ভি. মোহনার বেঞ্চে গ্রহণের (অ্যাডমিশন) জন্য তালিকাভুক্ত। আদালত সকাল 10:30-এ বসে। এর সঙ্গে সাতটি যুক্ত আবেদন তালিকাভুক্ত, তার মধ্যে আসাদউদ্দিন ওয়াইসি, রাহুল গান্ধী ও অন্যান্য, দিগ্বিজয় সিং এবং দোলা সেনের আবেদন রয়েছে।

list-04.matter: Petitions on Kerala's revision, heard with the matters on Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
list-04.due: On 30 October the Election Commission was given four weeks to file its counter affidavit and to answer the points in the petitioners' note.
list-04.quote: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने चुनाव आयोग को जवाबी हलफनामा दाखिल करने के लिए चार सप्ताह का समय दिया है।

hi.matter: केरल के पुनरीक्षण पर याचिकाएँ, जिनकी सुनवाई उत्तर प्रदेश और छत्तीसगढ़ के मामलों के साथ हुई।
hi.due: 30 अक्टूबर को निर्वाचन आयोग को अपना जवाबी हलफ़नामा दाखिल करने और याचिकाकर्ताओं के नोट के बिंदुओं का जवाब देने के लिए चार सप्ताह दिए गए।

ur.matter: کیرالہ کی نظرثانی پر درخواستیں، جن کی سماعت اتر پردیش اور چھتیس گڑھ کے معاملات کے ساتھ ہوئی۔
ur.due: 30 اکتوبر کو الیکشن کمیشن کو اپنا جوابی حلف نامہ داخل کرنے اور درخواست گزاروں کے نوٹ کے نکات کا جواب دینے کے لیے چار ہفتے دیے گئے۔

te.matter: కేరళ సవరణపై పిటిషన్లు. వీటిని ఉత్తరప్రదేశ్, ఛత్తీస్‌గఢ్ కేసులతో కలిపి విచారించారు.
te.due: అక్టోబర్ 30న ఎన్నికల సంఘానికి కౌంటర్ అఫిడవిట్ దాఖలు చేయడానికి, పిటిషనర్ల నోట్‌లోని అంశాలకు జవాబు ఇవ్వడానికి నాలుగు వారాలు ఇచ్చారు.

ta.matter: கேரள திருத்தம் குறித்த மனுக்கள். இவை உத்தரப் பிரதேசம், சத்தீஸ்கர் வழக்குகளுடன் சேர்த்து விசாரிக்கப்பட்டன.
ta.due: எதிர் பிரமாணப் பத்திரம் தாக்கல் செய்யவும் மனுதாரர்களின் குறிப்பில் உள்ள கேள்விகளுக்குப் பதில் அளிக்கவும் அக்டோபர் 30 அன்று தேர்தல் ஆணையத்துக்கு நான்கு வாரங்கள் வழங்கப்பட்டன.

bn.matter: কেরলের সংশোধন নিয়ে আবেদন, যার শুনানি উত্তরপ্রদেশ ও ছত্তীসগড়ের মামলার সঙ্গে হয়েছে।
bn.due: 30 অক্টোবর নির্বাচন কমিশনকে পাল্টা হলফনামা জমা দিতে এবং আবেদনকারীদের নোটের বিষয়গুলির জবাব দিতে চার সপ্তাহ দেওয়া হয়।

list-05.matter: Petitions against the exclusion of electors in Maharashtra's revision. The Election Commission asked for them to be deferred because the Supreme Court is hearing the revision.
list-05.due: The petitions are listed for hearing. The High Court has given no view on their merits.
list-05.quote: The Bombay High Court has fixed December 1 for hearing petitions that challenge alleged arbitrary exclusions of voters during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Maharashtra, after the Election Commission of India (ECI) sought a deferral

hi.matter: महाराष्ट्र के पुनरीक्षण में मतदाताओं को सूची से बाहर किए जाने के ख़िलाफ़ याचिकाएँ। निर्वाचन आयोग ने इन्हें टालने को कहा, क्योंकि सुप्रीम कोर्ट पुनरीक्षण की सुनवाई कर रहा है।
hi.due: याचिकाएँ सुनवाई के लिए सूचीबद्ध हैं। हाईकोर्ट ने इनके गुण-दोष पर कोई राय नहीं दी है।

ur.matter: مہاراشٹر کی نظرثانی میں ووٹروں کو فہرست سے باہر کیے جانے کے خلاف درخواستیں۔ الیکشن کمیشن نے انہیں ملتوی کرنے کو کہا، کیونکہ سپریم کورٹ نظرثانی کی سماعت کر رہی ہے۔
ur.due: درخواستیں سماعت کے لیے فہرست میں ہیں۔ ہائی کورٹ نے ان کی خوبیوں اور خامیوں پر کوئی رائے نہیں دی ہے۔

te.matter: మహారాష్ట్ర సవరణలో ఓటర్లను జాబితా నుంచి తప్పించడంపై పిటిషన్లు. సుప్రీంకోర్టు సవరణను విచారిస్తున్నందున వీటిని వాయిదా వేయాలని ఎన్నికల సంఘం కోరింది.
te.due: పిటిషన్లు విచారణకు జాబితాలో ఉన్నాయి. వాటి మంచిచెడులపై హైకోర్టు ఎలాంటి అభిప్రాయం చెప్పలేదు.

ta.matter: மகாராஷ்டிர திருத்தத்தில் வாக்காளர்கள் பட்டியலிலிருந்து விலக்கப்பட்டதை எதிர்த்த மனுக்கள். உச்ச நீதிமன்றம் திருத்தத்தை விசாரித்து வருவதால் இவற்றைத் தள்ளிவைக்கத் தேர்தல் ஆணையம் கேட்டது.
ta.due: மனுக்கள் விசாரணைக்குப் பட்டியலிடப்பட்டுள்ளன. அவற்றின் தகுதி குறித்து உயர் நீதிமன்றம் எந்தக் கருத்தும் தெரிவிக்கவில்லை.

bn.matter: মহারাষ্ট্রের সংশোধনে ভোটারদের তালিকা থেকে বাদ দেওয়ার বিরুদ্ধে আবেদন। সুপ্রিম কোর্ট সংশোধনের শুনানি করছে বলে নির্বাচন কমিশন এগুলি পিছিয়ে দিতে বলে।
bn.due: আবেদনগুলি শুনানির তালিকায় আছে। এগুলির গুণাগুণ নিয়ে হাইকোর্ট কোনো মত দেয়নি।

hi.matter: दिल्ली के पुनरीक्षण पर पारदर्शिता के लिए काम करने वाली दो कार्यकर्ताओं की याचिका, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, और फ़ॉर्म 6 पर आयोग के पत्र को लेकर वह आवेदन जिसे दाखिल करने को उनसे कहा गया।
hi.due: याचिका मुख्य न्यायाधीश की अदालत में आइटम 26 के रूप में दाखिले (एडमिशन) के लिए सूचीबद्ध है, मुख्य न्यायाधीश, जस्टिस जॉयमाल्य बागची और जस्टिस वी. मोहना की पीठ के सामने। स्पष्टीकरण या निर्देश के लिए एक आवेदन और एक हस्तक्षेप आवेदन उसके साथ हैं। एक जुड़ी हुई याचिका, W.P.(C) No. 1339 of 2026, उसके साथ आइटम 26.1 के रूप में सूचीबद्ध है। अदालत सुबह 10:30 बजे से बैठती है। 4 नवंबर को अदालत ने तुरंत कोई आदेश देने से इनकार किया और याचिकाकर्ताओं से इस तारीख़ से पहले अपना आवेदन दाखिल करने को कहा।

ur.matter: دہلی کی نظرثانی پر شفافیت کے لیے کام کرنے والی دو کارکنوں کی درخواست، W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026، اور فارم 6 کے بارے میں کمیشن کے خط پر وہ عرضی جو داخل کرنے کو ان سے کہا گیا۔
ur.due: درخواست چیف جسٹس کی عدالت میں آئٹم 26 کے طور پر داخلے کے لیے فہرست میں ہے، چیف جسٹس، جسٹس جوئے مالیہ باگچی اور جسٹس وی موہنا کی بنچ کے سامنے۔ وضاحت یا ہدایت کے لیے ایک عرضی اور مداخلت کی ایک عرضی اس کے ساتھ ہیں۔ ایک منسلک درخواست، W.P.(C) No. 1339 of 2026، اس کے ساتھ آئٹم 26.1 کے طور پر فہرست میں ہے۔ عدالت صبح 10:30 بجے سے بیٹھتی ہے۔ 4 نومبر کو عدالت نے فوری حکم دینے سے انکار کیا اور درخواست گزاروں سے اس تاریخ سے پہلے اپنی عرضی داخل کرنے کو کہا۔

te.matter: ఢిల్లీ సవరణపై పారదర్శకత కోసం పనిచేసే ఇద్దరు కార్యకర్తల పిటిషన్, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, ఫారం 6పై సంఘం లేఖ గురించి దాఖలు చేయమని వారికి చెప్పిన దరఖాస్తు.
te.due: పిటిషన్ ప్రధాన న్యాయమూర్తి కోర్టులో అంశం 26గా, ప్రధాన న్యాయమూర్తి, జస్టిస్ జోయ్‌మాల్య బాగ్చీ, జస్టిస్ వి. మోహన ధర్మాసనం ముందు అడ్మిషన్ కోసం జాబితాలో ఉంది. వివరణ లేదా ఆదేశం కోసం ఒక దరఖాస్తు, ఒక జోక్యం దరఖాస్తు దానితో ఉన్నాయి. ఒక అనుబంధ పిటిషన్, W.P.(C) No. 1339 of 2026, దానితో పాటు అంశం 26.1గా జాబితాలో ఉంది. కోర్టు ఉదయం 10:30కి ప్రారంభమవుతుంది. నవంబర్ 4న కోర్టు అత్యవసర ఉత్తర్వులు ఇవ్వడానికి నిరాకరించి, ఈ తేదీకి ముందు దరఖాస్తు దాఖలు చేయమని పిటిషనర్లకు చెప్పింది.

ta.matter: தில்லி திருத்தம் குறித்து வெளிப்படைத்தன்மைக்காகச் செயல்படும் இரண்டு செயற்பாட்டாளர்களின் மனு, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, மற்றும் படிவம் 6 குறித்த ஆணையத்தின் கடிதம் பற்றித் தாக்கல் செய்யுமாறு அவர்களிடம் கூறப்பட்ட விண்ணப்பம்.
ta.due: மனு தலைமை நீதிபதியின் நீதிமன்றத்தில் வரிசை எண் 26 ஆக, தலைமை நீதிபதி, நீதிபதி ஜாய்மால்யா பாக்சி, நீதிபதி வி. மோகனா அமர்வு முன் அனுமதிக்காகப் பட்டியலிடப்பட்டுள்ளது. விளக்கம் அல்லது வழிகாட்டுதல் கோரும் ஒரு விண்ணப்பமும் ஓர் இடையீட்டு விண்ணப்பமும் அதனுடன் உள்ளன. ஓர் இணைந்த மனு, W.P.(C) No. 1339 of 2026, அதனுடன் வரிசை எண் 26.1 ஆகப் பட்டியலிடப்பட்டுள்ளது. நீதிமன்றம் காலை 10:30 மணிக்குத் தொடங்குகிறது. நவம்பர் 4 அன்று நீதிமன்றம் அவசர உத்தரவு பிறப்பிக்க மறுத்து, இந்தத் தேதிக்கு முன் விண்ணப்பத்தைத் தாக்கல் செய்யுமாறு மனுதாரர்களிடம் கூறியது.

bn.matter: দিল্লির সংশোধন নিয়ে স্বচ্ছতার জন্য কাজ করা দুই কর্মীর আবেদন, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, এবং ফর্ম 6 নিয়ে কমিশনের চিঠি সম্পর্কে যে আবেদন দাখিল করতে তাঁদের বলা হয়েছে।
bn.due: আবেদনটি প্রধান বিচারপতির আদালতে 26 নম্বর আইটেম হিসেবে প্রধান বিচারপতি, বিচারপতি জয়মাল্য বাগচী ও বিচারপতি ভি. মোহনার বেঞ্চে গ্রহণের (অ্যাডমিশন) জন্য তালিকাভুক্ত। ব্যাখ্যা বা নির্দেশের জন্য একটি আবেদন এবং একটি হস্তক্ষেপের আবেদন এর সঙ্গে রয়েছে। একটি যুক্ত আবেদন, W.P.(C) No. 1339 of 2026, এর সঙ্গে 26.1 নম্বর আইটেম হিসেবে তালিকাভুক্ত। আদালত সকাল 10:30-এ বসে। 4 নভেম্বর আদালত জরুরি কোনো আদেশ দিতে অস্বীকার করে এবং আবেদনকারীদের এই তারিখের আগে তাঁদের আবেদন দাখিল করতে বলে।

ta.matter: தலைமைத் தேர்தல் ஆணையருக்கு எதிராக அக்டோபர் 12 அன்று எதிர்க்கட்சிகள் நடத்திய பேரணிக்குப் பின், உச்ச நீதிமன்றம் அருகே ஊர்வலங்கள் மற்றும் போராட்டங்களுக்கான வழிகாட்டுதல்கள் கோரி வழக்கறிஞர்கள் குழு தாக்கல் செய்த மனு.
ta.due: நவம்பர் 3 அன்று நீதிமன்றம் மல்லிகார்ஜுன கார்கே, ராகுல் காந்தி மற்றும் மத்திய அரசிடம் பதில் கோரியது. இந்தத் தேதிக்குள் பதில் அளிப்பதாக மத்திய அரசு கூறியது.
